// include/ops/helpers/ReductionKernels.cuh
// Unified GPU reduction kernel + config solver + offset calculator
// All in one file — these helpers are only used here, no need for separate headers.
#pragma once

#ifndef REDUCTION_KERNELS_CUH
#define REDUCTION_KERNELS_CUH

#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <cuda_fp16.h>
#include <cuda_bf16.h>
#include <device_launch_parameters.h>
#include <cstdint>
#include <algorithm>

#if defined(__CUDACC__) || defined(__HIPCC__)
// Constants for occupancy calculation based on architecture limits
// sm_75 (Turing): 1024 threads/SM
// sm_86/87/89 (Ampere): 1536 threads/SM
// sm_70/80 (Volta/A100): 2048 threads/SM
#if __CUDA_ARCH__ == 750
  #define CUDA_MAX_THREADS_PER_SM 1024
#elif __CUDA_ARCH__ == 860 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 870 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 890 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 1200
  #define CUDA_MAX_THREADS_PER_SM 1536
#else
  #define CUDA_MAX_THREADS_PER_SM 2048
#endif

#define GAU_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK 1024

// Clipping macro to ensure (threads * blocks) <= hardware limit
#define GAU_MIN_BLOCKS_PER_SM(threads_per_block, blocks_per_sm)        \
  ((((threads_per_block) * (blocks_per_sm) <= CUDA_MAX_THREADS_PER_SM) \
        ? (blocks_per_sm)                                              \
        : ((CUDA_MAX_THREADS_PER_SM + (threads_per_block) - 1) /       \
           (threads_per_block))))
#endif

// gpu_isnan, gpu_add, gpu_mul, gpu_lt, gpu_gt are ALL defined in ReductionOps.h
// under #ifdef __CUDA_ARCH__ — no need to re-declare them here.
#include "ReductionOps.h"
#include "ReductionUtils.h"  // For ReductionLayout
#include "device/AllocatorRegistry.h"  // multi-CTA staging buffer alloc

namespace OwnTensor {
namespace cuda {

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// TYPE CONVERSIONS (wrappers for __half / __nv_bfloat16)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

template<typename T> __device__ float to_float(T val) { return static_cast<float>(val); }
template<> __device__ float to_float(__half val)        { return __half2float(val); }
template<> __device__ float to_float(__nv_bfloat16 val) { return __bfloat162float(val); }

template<typename T> __device__ T from_float(float val) { return static_cast<T>(val); }
template<> __device__ __half       from_float(float val) { return __float2half(val); }
template<> __device__ __nv_bfloat16 from_float(float val) { return __float2bfloat16(val); }

} // namespace cuda

namespace detail {

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 1: GPU REDUCE CONFIG
// Mirrors PyTorch's ReduceConfig (Reduce.cuh:73-217)
// Decides block/grid dimensions based on the problem shape.
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// Max live threads per block — conservative so we don't miss occupancy
template<typename T>
struct MaxThreads { static constexpr int VALUE = 512; };

// Helpers: round to powers of 2
inline int next_pow2(int x) {
    if (x <= 0) return 1;
    --x;
    x |= x >> 1; x |= x >> 2; x |= x >> 4; x |= x >> 8; x |= x >> 16;
    return x + 1;
}
inline int last_pow2(int x)   { return next_pow2(x + 1) / 2; }
inline int div_up(int a, int b){ return (a + b - 1) / b; }

struct GpuReduceConfig {
    static constexpr int BLOCK_X = 0;
    static constexpr int BLOCK_Y = 1;
    static constexpr int CTA     = 2;

    int element_size_bytes;
    int num_inputs;           // reduced_count: elements per output
    int num_outputs;          // independent outputs
    int step_input  = 1;
    int step_output = 1;
    int ctas_per_output = 1;
    int input_mult[3]  = {0, 0, 0};
    int output_mult[2] = {0, 0};
    int block_width  = 1;
    int block_height = 1;
    int num_threads  = 1;
    bool vectorize_input = false;
    int  output_vec_size = 1;

    GpuReduceConfig() = default;
    GpuReduceConfig(int esz, int nout, int nin)
        : element_size_bytes(esz), num_inputs(nin), num_outputs(nout) {}

    // Set block_width × block_height so it fits max_num_threads
    template<typename T>
    void set_block_dimension(int64_t dim0, int64_t dim1) {
        const int max_t = MaxThreads<T>::VALUE / output_vec_size;
        int d0 = dim0 < max_t ? static_cast<int>(last_pow2(dim0)) : max_t;
        int d1 = dim1 < max_t ? static_cast<int>(last_pow2(dim1)) : max_t;
        block_width  = std::min(d0, 32);
        block_height = std::min(d1, max_t / block_width);
        block_width  = std::min(d0, max_t / block_height);
        num_threads  = block_width * block_height;
    }

    int split_input (int p) { int s = step_input;  step_input  *= p; return s; }
    int split_output(int p) { int s = step_output; step_output *= p; return s; }

    dim3 block() const { return dim3(block_width, block_height); }
    dim3 grid()  const { return dim3(div_up(num_outputs / output_vec_size, step_output), ctas_per_output); }

    __host__ __device__ bool should_block_x_reduce() const { return input_mult[BLOCK_X] != 0; }
    __host__ __device__ bool should_block_y_reduce() const { return input_mult[BLOCK_Y] != 0; }
    __host__ __device__ bool should_global_reduce()  const { return input_mult[CTA]     != 0; }

    int shared_memory_size() const {
        if (!should_block_y_reduce() && (!should_block_x_reduce() || block_width <= 32))
            return 0;
        return element_size_bytes * num_threads * output_vec_size;
    }
    int values_per_thread() const { return div_up(num_inputs, step_input); }
    int semaphore_size()    const {
        return should_global_reduce() ? (int)(sizeof(int) * grid().x) : 0;
    }
};

// Host-side solver — mirrors PyTorch's setReduceConfig()
// Call this ONCE on the host before launching the kernel.
template<typename acc_t>
GpuReduceConfig build_reduce_config(const ReductionLayout& layout, int num_mp, int max_threads_per_mp) {
    int num_outputs       = static_cast<int>(layout.num_outputs);
    int inputs_per_output = static_cast<int>(layout.reduced_count);

    // OuterContiguous: inner_count is the "fast" dimension (outputs),
    // num_outputs is how many rows we reduce over.
    if (layout.path == ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous) {
        num_outputs       = static_cast<int>(layout.inner_count);
        inputs_per_output = static_cast<int>(layout.reduced_count);
    } else if (layout.path == ReductionLayout::Path::Generic) {
        if (num_outputs       == 0) num_outputs       = 1;
        if (inputs_per_output == 0) inputs_per_output = 1;
    }

    auto config = GpuReduceConfig(sizeof(acc_t), num_outputs, inputs_per_output);
    bool inner = (layout.path != ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous);

    int64_t dim0 = inner ? inputs_per_output : num_outputs;
    int64_t dim1 = inner ? num_outputs       : inputs_per_output;
    config.set_block_dimension<acc_t>(dim0, dim1);

    int bw = config.block_width, bh = config.block_height;

    if (inner) config.input_mult[0]  = config.split_input(bw);
    else       config.output_mult[0] = config.split_output(bw);

    constexpr int min_vpt = 16, max_vpt = 256;
    bool split_warps = config.values_per_thread() >= std::min<int>(bh * 16, max_vpt);
    if (split_warps) config.input_mult[1]  = config.split_input(bh);
    else             config.output_mult[1] = config.split_output(bh);

    // Multi-CTA global reduce?
    const int blocks_per_sm = max_threads_per_mp / config.num_threads;
    const int target_grid   = num_mp * blocks_per_sm;
    int gx = config.grid().x;
    if (config.input_mult[1] != 0 && config.values_per_thread() >= max_vpt && gx <= target_grid) {
        int cpo = std::max(
            std::min<int>(div_up(target_grid, gx), div_up(config.values_per_thread(), min_vpt)),
            div_up(config.values_per_thread(), max_vpt));
        config.ctas_per_output = cpo;
        if (cpo > 1) config.input_mult[2] = config.split_input(cpo);
    }
    return config;
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 2: OFFSET CALCULATOR
// Generic N-D stride-based index → byte offset.
// Used only by the Generic fallback tier (~5% of DL cases).
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

template<int NARGS = 1, typename index_t = uint32_t>
struct OffsetCalculator {
    static constexpr int MAX_DIMS = 10;
    int     dims;
    index_t sizes[MAX_DIMS];
    index_t strides[NARGS][MAX_DIMS];

    __host__ __device__ OffsetCalculator() : dims(0) {}

    __host__ __device__ OffsetCalculator(int dims, const int64_t* shape,
                                          const int64_t* const* strides_arr) : dims(dims) {
        for (int i = 0; i < dims && i < MAX_DIMS; i++) {
            this->sizes[i] = static_cast<index_t>(shape[i]);
            for (int j = 0; j < NARGS; j++)
                this->strides[j][i] = static_cast<index_t>(strides_arr[j][i]);
        }
    }

    // O(ndim) div/mod — only called on the Generic (5%) path
    __host__ __device__ index_t get(index_t linear_idx, int arg = 0) const {
        index_t offset = 0;
        for (int d = dims - 1; d >= 0; d--) {
            index_t coord  = linear_idx % sizes[d];
            linear_idx    /= sizes[d];
            offset        += coord * strides[arg][d];
        }
        return offset;
    }
};

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 3: PACKED REDUCE OP STRUCT
// Packs all kernel arguments into a single struct to minimize
// cudaLaunchKernel parameter overhead (like PyTorch's ReduceOp).
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

template<typename scalar_t, typename out_scalar_t, typename ops_t, typename index_t = uint32_t>
struct ReduceOp {
    ops_t ops;
    GpuReduceConfig config;
    OffsetCalculator<1, index_t> input_calc;
    OffsetCalculator<1, index_t> output_calc;
    const scalar_t*  __restrict__ src;
    out_scalar_t*    __restrict__ dst;
    int64_t step_stride;
    // Multi-CTA staging (populated only when config.should_global_reduce()).
    // cta_buf: num_outputs * ctas_per_output * sizeof(arg_t), uninitialised.
    // semaphores: num_outputs ints, zero-initialised by host before launch.
    void* cta_buf    = nullptr;
    int*  semaphores = nullptr;
};

} // namespace detail

namespace cuda {

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 4: WARP / BLOCK REDUCE STAGES
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// Block-X reduce: all threads in a row collaborate to reduce input
// Uses warp shuffles first (register), then shared memory for cross-warp.
template<typename arg_t, typename ops_t>
__device__ arg_t block_x_reduce(arg_t value, const ops_t& ops, char* shared_memory) {
    int lane = threadIdx.x % 32;
    int wid  = threadIdx.x / 32;

    // Warp-level shuffle reduction
    #pragma unroll
    for (int offset = 16; offset > 0; offset /= 2)
        value = ops.combine(value, ops.warp_shfl_down(value, offset));

    // Write warp leader to shared memory
    arg_t* smem = reinterpret_cast<arg_t*>(shared_memory);
    if (lane == 0) smem[wid] = value;
    __syncthreads();

    // First warp reduces across all warp results
    if (wid == 0) {
        value = (threadIdx.x < blockDim.x / 32) ? smem[lane] : ops.identity();
        #pragma unroll
        for (int offset = 16; offset > 0; offset /= 2)
            value = ops.combine(value, ops.warp_shfl_down(value, offset));
    }
    return value;
}

// Block-Y reduce: threads in the same column (same threadIdx.x) reduce
// across all Y rows using shared memory.
template<typename arg_t, typename ops_t>
__device__ arg_t block_y_reduce(arg_t value, const ops_t& ops, char* shared_memory) {
    arg_t* smem = reinterpret_cast<arg_t*>(shared_memory);
    smem[threadIdx.x + threadIdx.y * blockDim.x] = value;
    __syncthreads();

    if (threadIdx.y == 0) {
        value = smem[threadIdx.x];
        for (int i = 1; i < blockDim.y; i++)
            value = ops.combine(value, smem[threadIdx.x + i * blockDim.x]);
    }
    return value;
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 5: UNIFIED REDUCTION KERNEL
// Templated on Path to eliminate runtime branching.
// Uses vectorized loads (vt0 elements per iteration) and
// multiple independent accumulators for ILP.
//
// Template params:
//   scalar_t      — input element type (after CudaNativeType conversion)
//   out_scalar_t  — output element type
//   ops_t         — functor (SumOp, MinOp, ArgMinOp, MeanOps, WelfordOps, ...)
//   index_t       — indexing width (uint32_t for tensors < 4GB)
//   PATH          — compile-time path selection (no runtime branching)
//   NT            — num_threads for __launch_bounds__
//   VT0           — values per thread for ILP (default 4)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

// Vectorized load helper: load VT0 elements as a single wide transaction
template<typename T, int N>
struct alignas(sizeof(T) * N) VecLoad {
    T val[N];
};

// Compile-time min-blocks-per-SM based on num_threads:
//   512 threads → 4 blocks/SM (2048 threads/SM)
//   256 threads → 8 blocks/SM
//   128 threads → 4 blocks/SM (conservative — high register kernels)
//   64  threads → 4 blocks/SM
//   32  threads → 4 blocks/SM
// Capped at 4 to avoid ptxas spilling registers trying to satisfy
// an unreachable occupancy target for complex functors (WelfordOps, etc).
// The compiler will still achieve higher occupancy when registers allow.
// Capped at hardware limit to ensure valid occupancy and avoid warnings (sm_86: 1536 threads/SM).
template<int NT>
struct MinBlocksPerSM {
    static constexpr int requested = (NT >= 256) ? (2048 / NT) : 4;
    static constexpr int VALUE = GAU_MIN_BLOCKS_PER_SM(NT, requested);
};

template<typename scalar_t, typename out_scalar_t, typename ops_t, typename index_t,
         detail::ReductionLayout::Path PATH, int NT, int VT0 = 4>
__launch_bounds__(NT, MinBlocksPerSM<NT>::VALUE)
__global__ void unified_reduce_kernel(detail::ReduceOp<scalar_t, out_scalar_t, ops_t, index_t> op) {
    extern __shared__ char shared_memory[];

    // accumulator type is whatever the functor's identity() returns
    using arg_t = decltype(op.ops.identity());
    const auto& config = op.config;

    // ── 1. Map this thread to an output index ──
    index_t output_idx =
        (index_t)threadIdx.x * config.output_mult[detail::GpuReduceConfig::BLOCK_X] +
        (index_t)threadIdx.y * config.output_mult[detail::GpuReduceConfig::BLOCK_Y] +
        (index_t)blockIdx.x  * config.step_output;

    if (output_idx >= (index_t)config.num_outputs) return;

    // ── 2. Map this thread to its starting input index ──
    // input_mult[CTA] term: when ctas_per_output > 1, each block along grid.y
    // owns a disjoint slice of the reduced axis. Without this term, all CTAs
    // for a given output_idx would walk the same range (the multi-CTA bug).
    index_t idx =
        (index_t)threadIdx.x * config.input_mult[detail::GpuReduceConfig::BLOCK_X] +
        (index_t)threadIdx.y * config.input_mult[detail::GpuReduceConfig::BLOCK_Y] +
        (index_t)blockIdx.y  * config.input_mult[detail::GpuReduceConfig::CTA];

    const index_t end    = (index_t)config.num_inputs;
    const index_t stride = (index_t)config.step_input;

    // ── 3. Thread-local reduction with ILP (VT0 independent accumulators) ──
    // Multiple accumulators hide the latency of dependent reduce operations.
    arg_t acc[VT0];
    #pragma unroll
    for (int i = 0; i < VT0; i++) acc[i] = op.ops.identity();

    if constexpr (PATH == detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous) {
        // TIER 1: Contiguous – stride=1, output × reduced_count laid out linearly.
        // Covers ~70% of DL workloads (e.g. sum(axis=-1) on row-major tensors).
        const scalar_t* __restrict__ base_ptr = op.src + output_idx * (index_t)config.num_inputs;

        // Vectorized main loop: load VT0 elements per iteration
        while (idx + (VT0 - 1) * stride < end) {
            #pragma unroll
            for (int i = 0; i < VT0; i++) {
                acc[i] = op.ops.reduce(acc[i], base_ptr[idx + i * stride], (int64_t)(idx + i * stride));
            }
            idx += stride * VT0;
        }
        // Scalar tail
        while (idx < end) {
            acc[0] = op.ops.reduce(acc[0], base_ptr[idx], (int64_t)idx);
            idx += stride;
        }
    }
    else if constexpr (PATH == detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous) {
        // TIER 2: Single-stride – output dimension is innermost, reduced dim is outer.
        // Covers ~25% of DL workloads (e.g. sum(axis=0) on NCHW → C).
        const scalar_t* __restrict__ base_ptr = op.src + output_idx;
        const index_t row_stride = (index_t)op.step_stride;

        // ILP main loop: VT0 independent accumulators, strided access
        while (idx + (VT0 - 1) * stride < end) {
            #pragma unroll
            for (int i = 0; i < VT0; i++) {
                acc[i] = op.ops.reduce(acc[i], base_ptr[(idx + i * stride) * row_stride], (int64_t)(idx + i * stride));
            }
            idx += stride * VT0;
        }
        // Scalar tail
        while (idx < end) {
            acc[0] = op.ops.reduce(acc[0], base_ptr[idx * row_stride], (int64_t)idx);
            idx += stride;
        }
    }
    else {
        // TIER 3: Generic fallback — uses OffsetCalculator (O(ndim) div/mod).
        // Covers ~5% of cases: non-standard axes, non-contiguous or permuted tensors.
        index_t out_base = (op.output_calc.dims > 0)
            ? op.output_calc.get(output_idx)
            : output_idx;

        // ILP main loop for generic path
        while (idx + (VT0 - 1) * stride < end) {
            #pragma unroll
            for (int i = 0; i < VT0; i++) {
                index_t cur = idx + i * stride;
                index_t in_off = (op.input_calc.dims > 0) ? op.input_calc.get(cur) : cur;
                acc[i] = op.ops.reduce(acc[i], op.src[out_base + in_off], (int64_t)cur);
            }
            idx += stride * VT0;
        }
        // Scalar tail
        while (idx < end) {
            index_t in_off = (op.input_calc.dims > 0) ? op.input_calc.get(idx) : idx;
            acc[0] = op.ops.reduce(acc[0], op.src[out_base + in_off], (int64_t)idx);
            idx += stride;
        }
    }

    // ── 4. Combine VT0 accumulators into acc[0] ──
    #pragma unroll
    for (int i = 1; i < VT0; i++) {
        acc[0] = op.ops.combine(acc[0], acc[i]);
    }

    arg_t value = acc[0];

    // ── 5. Block-level map-reduce stages ──
    if (config.should_block_x_reduce())
        value = block_x_reduce(value, op.ops, shared_memory);
    if (config.should_block_y_reduce())
        value = block_y_reduce(value, op.ops, shared_memory);

    // ── 6. Write output ──
    bool is_leader = (!config.should_block_x_reduce() || threadIdx.x == 0) &&
                     (!config.should_block_y_reduce() || threadIdx.y == 0);

    // ── 6a. Multi-CTA path — line-by-line port of PyTorch ReduceOp::global_reduce
    //                       (aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Reduce.cuh:786-870).
    //
    // Invariant entering this block: `value` is the per-CTA block-reduced partial
    // (post block_x_reduce AND block_y_reduce). For threads where !is_leader the
    // contents of `value` are stale/garbage — that is OK, only is_leader threads
    // stage and only the last CTA reads back from staging.
    //
    // Staging layout (matches PT's staging_memory_offset):
    //   block_x_reduce ON  : slot = blockIdx.y + blockIdx.x*gridDim.y
    //                        (1 slot per CTA)
    //   block_x_reduce OFF : slot = threadIdx.x + (blockIdx.y + blockIdx.x*gridDim.y) * blockDim.x
    //                        (blockDim.x slots per CTA — one per output column held by lane tx)
    //
    // Semaphores: one int per blockIdx.x tile, zero-initialised by the host.
    if (config.should_global_reduce()) {
        arg_t* cta_buf = reinterpret_cast<arg_t*>(op.cta_buf);

        auto staging_offset = [&](index_t cta2) -> index_t {
            index_t off = cta2 + (index_t)blockIdx.x * (index_t)gridDim.y;
            if (!config.should_block_x_reduce())
                off = (index_t)threadIdx.x + off * (index_t)blockDim.x;
            return off;
        };

        // (1) Stage: every is_leader thread writes its (block-reduced) partial
        //     for this CTA at slot staging_offset(blockIdx.y).
        if (is_leader) {
            cta_buf[staging_offset((index_t)blockIdx.y)] = value;
        }
        __threadfence();   // store must be globally visible before atomicAdd
        __syncthreads();

        // (2) Last-CTA detection — one atomic per output-column tile (blockIdx.x).
        __shared__ bool s_is_last;
        if (threadIdx.x == 0 && threadIdx.y == 0) {
            int prev = atomicAdd(&op.semaphores[blockIdx.x], 1);
            s_is_last = (prev == config.ctas_per_output - 1);
        }
        __syncthreads();
        if (!s_is_last) return;

        __threadfence();   // acquire pattern after the atomic: pair with the
                           // producer's __threadfence above.

        // (3) Every thread in the last CTA resets to identity and re-reads its
        //     slice of the staging buffer, combining cpo partials in parallel.
        //     Iteration pattern mirrors PT's global_reduce loop.
        value = op.ops.identity();
        if (config.should_block_x_reduce()) {
            // Each thread covers a strided subset of [0, cpo).
            index_t input_offset = (index_t)threadIdx.x + (index_t)threadIdx.y * (index_t)blockDim.x;
            index_t step = (index_t)blockDim.x * (index_t)blockDim.y;
            for (; input_offset < (index_t)config.ctas_per_output; input_offset += step) {
                value = op.ops.combine(value, cta_buf[staging_offset(input_offset)]);
            }
        } else {
            // Each (tx, ty) reads slots {tx + (ty + bx*gd.y)*bd.x, tx + (ty+bd.y + bx*gd.y)*bd.x, …}
            // i.e. each lane reconstructs its own output column from cpo partials,
            // distributed across the y-dim threads of the last CTA.
            index_t input_offset = (index_t)threadIdx.y;
            index_t step = (index_t)blockDim.y;
            for (; input_offset < (index_t)config.ctas_per_output; input_offset += step) {
                value = op.ops.combine(value, cta_buf[staging_offset(input_offset)]);
            }
        }

        // (4) Final block-level reductions over the y (and possibly x) dim so
        //     only the is_leader thread holds the full sum for its output_idx.
        value = block_y_reduce(value, op.ops, shared_memory);
        if (config.should_block_x_reduce())
            value = block_x_reduce(value, op.ops, shared_memory);

        // (5) Same write rule as the single-CTA path.
        if (is_leader && output_idx < (index_t)config.num_outputs) {
            auto final_val = op.ops.project(value);
            if constexpr (std::is_same_v<out_scalar_t, __half>)
                op.dst[output_idx] = from_float<out_scalar_t>(static_cast<float>(final_val));
            else
                op.dst[output_idx] = static_cast<out_scalar_t>(final_val);
        }
        return;
    }

    // ── 6b. Single-CTA path (unchanged): leader writes dst directly ──
    if (is_leader) {
        auto final_val = op.ops.project(value);

        if constexpr (std::is_same_v<out_scalar_t, __half>)
            op.dst[output_idx] = from_float<out_scalar_t>(static_cast<float>(final_val));
        else
            op.dst[output_idx] = static_cast<out_scalar_t>(final_val);
    }
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// SECTION 6: HOST-SIDE KERNEL LAUNCHER
// Resolves Path at compile time and dispatches to the correct
// kernel specialization. Packs args into ReduceOp struct.
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

template<typename scalar_t, typename out_scalar_t, typename ops_t, typename index_t = uint32_t, int VT0 = 4>
inline void launch_reduce_kernel(
    const ops_t& ops,
    const detail::GpuReduceConfig& config,
    const detail::OffsetCalculator<1, index_t>& input_calc,
    const detail::OffsetCalculator<1, index_t>& output_calc,
    const scalar_t* src,
    out_scalar_t* dst,
    detail::ReductionLayout::Path path,
    int64_t step_stride,
    int smem,
    cudaStream_t stream)
{
    // Pack into single struct for minimal launch parameter overhead
    detail::ReduceOp<scalar_t, out_scalar_t, ops_t, index_t> op;
    op.ops = ops;
    op.config = config;
    op.input_calc = input_calc;
    op.output_calc = output_calc;
    op.src = src;
    op.dst = dst;
    op.step_stride = step_stride;

    // Multi-CTA staging: allocate cta_buf (uninit) and semaphores (zero-init).
    // Sized exactly like PyTorch's: num_outputs*ctas_per_output accumulators and
    // num_outputs ints. Uses the caching allocator so repeated launches reuse
    // the same blocks — no per-call cudaMalloc/cudaFree.
    using arg_t = decltype(ops.identity());
    Allocator* scratch = nullptr;
    if (config.should_global_reduce()) {
        scratch = AllocatorRegistry::get_caching_allocator();
        const dim3 g = config.grid();
        // cta_buf sizing (matches PyTorch's global_memory_size):
        //   1 slot per (CTA-x, CTA-y) when block_x_reduce is active
        //   blockDim.x slots per (CTA-x, CTA-y) otherwise (each lane reconstructs its own column)
        size_t slots = static_cast<size_t>(g.x) * static_cast<size_t>(g.y);
        if (!config.should_block_x_reduce()) {
            slots *= static_cast<size_t>(config.block_width);
        }
        size_t cta_bytes = sizeof(arg_t) * slots;
        size_t sem_bytes = sizeof(int)   * static_cast<size_t>(g.x);
        op.cta_buf    = scratch->allocate(cta_bytes);
        op.semaphores = reinterpret_cast<int*>(scratch->allocate(sem_bytes));
        cudaMemsetAsync(op.semaphores, 0, sem_bytes, stream);
    }

    const int nt = config.num_threads;

    // Dispatch on Path at compile time + num_threads for launch_bounds.
    // Using a lambda to avoid duplicating the grid/block/smem logic.
    #define LAUNCH_KERNEL(PATH_ENUM, NT_VAL) \
        unified_reduce_kernel<scalar_t, out_scalar_t, ops_t, index_t, PATH_ENUM, NT_VAL, VT0> \
            <<<config.grid(), config.block(), smem, stream>>>(op)

    if (path == detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous) {
        if      (nt <= 32)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous, 32);  }
        else if (nt <= 64)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous, 64);  }
        else if (nt <= 128) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous, 128); }
        else if (nt <= 256) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous, 256); }
        else                { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::InnerContiguous, 512); }
    }
    else if (path == detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous) {
        if      (nt <= 32)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous, 32);  }
        else if (nt <= 64)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous, 64);  }
        else if (nt <= 128) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous, 128); }
        else if (nt <= 256) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous, 256); }
        else                { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::OuterContiguous, 512); }
    }
    else {
        if      (nt <= 32)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::Generic, 32);  }
        else if (nt <= 64)  { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::Generic, 64);  }
        else if (nt <= 128) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::Generic, 128); }
        else if (nt <= 256) { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::Generic, 256); }
        else                { LAUNCH_KERNEL(detail::ReductionLayout::Path::Generic, 512); }
    }

    #undef LAUNCH_KERNEL

    // Return scratch blocks to the caching allocator. The allocator pools them
    // for reuse on the next launch, so this is essentially free.
    if (scratch) {
        scratch->deallocate(op.cta_buf);
        scratch->deallocate(op.semaphores);
    }
}

} // namespace cuda
} // namespace OwnTensor

#endif // REDUCTION_KERNELS_CUH

### #19 Packed SDPA — fully wired, both branches present

In [gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:211-228](BluTrain/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L211):
```cpp

}();

    merged = autograd::scaled_dot_product_attention_packed(qkv, n_heads_, ...);
```

- `mem_efficient_bwd_unified_kernel_exp12`: **3,840 inst** — packed backward, writes dQ/dK/dV directly into packed dqkv via `skip_grad_zero=true`.

### CLAUDE [2026-05-13 19:48 IST]

Let me trace each precisely.

### The 116 `cat_batched_kernel` — all 116 are token-gen

- **Only one `Tensor::cat` call site in the entire trainer** ([gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:969](BluTrain/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L969)) — the token-sampling loop.
- 2 generation events × 58 cat iterations = **116 exact match**. ✓

If even one cat were from somewhere else (e.g. attention/MLP), the count would be 116+something. It's clean 116. **100% token-gen.**

### The 116 `strided_inner_vec_copy_kernel` — also token-gen, but a different mechanism

Key observation: it's `<float4, float, 4>` — operates on **float** data, not int. Token tensors (`xgen`, `next_token`) are `int64_t`, so they can't be the source.

The count `116` matches a different number: **`model.forward(xgen)` runs 58 times per generation event × 2 events = 116 forwards.** Each forward through GPT-2 (under packed SDPA) goes through the LM head:

```cpp
// gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:~1495
Tensor w_T = autograd::transpose(wte.weight, 0, 1);     // [V,C] → view [C,V], non-contig
Tensor logits = autograd::matmul(x, w_T);                // forces .contiguous() inside matmul prep
```

The `transpose` produces a non-contiguous view. The subsequent matmul calls `.contiguous()` on it, which hits `Tensor::contiguous() → ContiguousKernel`. For this stride pattern the dispatcher picks the **`strided_inner_vec_copy_kernel<float4, float, 4>`** fast path (it's the vec-inner-dim case — the doc says ~70% of DL cases hit this tier).

So:
- **1 strided_inner_vec_copy per forward** × **116 forwards in token gen** = **116 exact match.** ✓

(Note: during TRAINING forwards/backwards, this same LM-head transpose copy *also* would have fired — but it gets dwarfed by the multi-CTA reductions/GEMMs and counts much higher. Or, more likely, training-time forwards go through `Tensor::contiguous()`'s short-circuit because the tensor was last touched in a way that left it contiguous via smart-reshape. Token-gen's sequential decoding pattern hits the slow path 116 times.)

### Are these related to packed SDPA?

**No — neither is.** Packed SDPA eliminated the *attention-internal* `make_shards_inplace + reshape + transpose + cat` traffic. It does NOT touch:
- The `Tensor::cat({xgen, next_token}, 1)` in the sampling loop (different code path entirely)
- The LM head's `transpose(wte.weight) → matmul` flow (independent of SDPA)

You'd see the same 116 + 116 with `USE_PACKED_SDPA=0` too. Try it — they'll be unchanged. The DIFFERENCE between SDPA=1 and SDPA=0 will show up in *other* kernels (`transpose_3d_tiled_kernel`, additional `generic_strided_copy_kernel`, etc. from per-attention-block shard/reshape/transpose).

### Are they needed?

| Block | Needed for training math? | Needed for diagnostic output? |
|---|---|---|
| `Tensor::cat` in sampling loop | No | Yes — only way to build up generated sequence |
| LM-head `transpose+matmul` during forward | **Yes** during training (loss needs logits) | Yes (sampling needs probabilities) |

The 116 strided copies aren't a separate "feature" — they're an unavoidable consequence of the **transposed LM-head matmul** firing 116 times during token-gen forwards. To eliminate them you'd need to either:
- (a) Skip token-gen entirely (you don't need it for benchmarking),
- (b) Cache the contiguous transposed weight so it's only built once per generation event (a real optimization — would drop 116 → 2),
- (c) Use a fused `matmul_transposed` op that doesn't need a contiguous transposed copy.

(b) is what PyTorch does internally (caches a contiguous LM-head buffer when weight-tying is on, sometimes).

### Practical answer to "are they needed?"

For your current profiling workflow: **no, they're noise.** Token-gen is purely diagnostic. The cat + strided copies don't affect any optimization metric we're measuring.

For real training runs: they fire only 5 times across 19k steps (TOK_GEN_FREQ=5000) → ~25s total → negligible. Keep them.

The decision to comment-out token-gen is **purely about cleaner profiling logs**, not about correctness or training perf. Up to you.

## Packed SDPA — fully verified, working as designed

### Numerical correctness — identical math

| Step | WITH packed | WITHOUT packed |
|---|---|---|

| 2 | loss 9.899070 | loss **9.899078** |

### Kernel-level proof — packed path eliminates exactly what doc §16 claims

Kernels that appear **only without packed**:

| Kernel | WITH | WITHOUT | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

### What I added

2. **Fast-path dispatch** at the top of `cuda_addmm`:
   ```cpp
   if (output.dtype()==fp32 && beta==1.0f && tb==1 && input.numel()==N
       && supported_layout(mat1, mat2, output)) {
       if (try_addmm_lt_bias_f32(...)) return;   // fused success
   }
   // else fall through to existing broadcast_scale + cublasGemmEx path
   ```

Eligibility = the **standard Linear+bias case in GPT-2** (fp32, beta=1.0, no batch dim around the matmul, 1D bias of length N, supported transpose layout). Everything else (other dtypes, beta ≠ 1, batched matmul, non-1D bias) falls through to the legacy path — zero-risk.

### Layout setup — mirrors the existing `cublasGemmEx` ordering

The existing path calls `cublasGemmEx(opB, opA, N, M, K, mat2, ldb, mat1, lda, output, ldc)` — the standard row-major-via-col-major-transpose trick. My Lt call uses the same convention:
- `TRANSA = opB`, `TRANSB = opA`
- Layout A ↔ `mat2` (M=N or K rows × K or N cols, ld=ldb)
- Layout B ↔ `mat1` (K or M rows × M or K cols, ld=lda)
- Layout C ↔ output (N rows × M cols, ld=ldc)

So Lt does exactly the same `(mat1 @ mat2)` computation, with the bias-add fused into the epilogue.

`Tensor-Implementations/Makefile:88` already has `-lcublasLt`, and the trainer transitively gets it via `libtensor.so` (just like `FusedLinearGelu_sm89.cu` does today). **No Makefile changes needed.**

### CLAUDE [2026-05-13 21:02 IST]

# End of Day Report — May 13, 2025

Hey team, here's a summary of what I worked on today on the BluTrain trainer.

## The big picture

I spent the day going through our sprint optimizations one by one and verifying whether each one is actually present in the BluTrain repo and actually being used by the training script. Along the way I fixed a handful of things that had silently regressed during the merge into BluTrain, and I also closed out a serious bias-gradient bug that a colleague had documented in HANDOFF.md.

## First, the small wires that were loose in BluTrain

I started with the optimizer's `zero_grad` function. The fast version that batches all gradient zero-outs into a single multi-tensor kernel was present in the codebase, but the function in `Optim.cpp` was still using the slow loop that fires one launch per parameter. I swapped the body to call `cuda::multi_tensor_zero_cuda(gpu_grads)` instead. After this, every training step launches about 4 zero kernels instead of 148. The cudaLaunchKernel count dropped, the kernel `multi_tensor_zero_sm89_kernel` started showing up in the profile with around 117 instances, and per-step time improved by roughly 30 to 40 milliseconds.

Then I went to the gradient clipping path. The trainer was calling the synchronous `clip_grad_norm_` function, which ends with a blocking `cudaMemcpy` that waits for the GPU to finish so it can read the final norm into a host variable. There's already an async version sitting in the code that uses `cudaMemcpyAsync` into pinned host memory, but nobody was calling it. I allocated a pinned float buffer once before the training loop, switched the call to `clip_grad_norm_async_`, and displayed the norm with a one-step lag (because if you try to read it immediately you have to sync, which defeats the whole point). After rebuild, the synchronous `cudaMemcpy` row completely disappeared from the API summary. The norm in the printed step line now reads `nan` on step 0 (a sentinel) and shows the previous step's value from step 1 onward. Math is identical otherwise.

## Cleaning up the trainer noise for profiling

The trainer was running the HellaSwag eval block at step 0 and the last step, which alone fires about 10,000 forward passes during evaluation and adds tens of thousands of extra kernel launches to the profile. I commented out all seven HellaSwag touch points in `gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp`, including the include, the load block, the CSV header column, the variable declaration, the eval call, the CSV row write, and the per-step reset. After this, the `sum_reduction_kernel` count dropped from 81,000 to about 104, and several other kernels that were being inflated by HellaSwag forwards collapsed by 20 to 150 times. Step 0 wall time dropped from 53 seconds to 13 seconds.

Then I noticed checkpointing was still running. Even with `config.checkpointing = false`, the `CheckpointManager` constructor and the shutdown `wait_for_completion` call were always executing because they were not gated by the flag. I commented out the constructor, the resume block, the save call inside the val block, and the shutdown flush, and set the flag to false for hygiene. This stopped the trainer from auto-resuming from a stale checkpoint file that was left over from earlier runs and cleaned up another small bit of profile noise.

## The activations and LayerNorm work

I checked the GeLU sm89 kernels and they were already correct and identical to the master reference, so nothing to do there. The doc claimed that ReLU was rewritten as a branch-free formula `(x + |x|) * 0.5` but in BluTrain it was still using the old ternary form, so I rewrote both the forward and backward to be branch-free. Doesn't affect GPT-2 since GPT-2 uses GeLU, but the doc was lying about the state of the code.

The `fused_bias_gelu` kernel was fp32-only in BluTrain even though the doc claimed it was templated for fp16 and bf16. I templated the forward kernel, the backward grad-input kernel, and the bias-reduce kernel, then added overloads of the launcher for `__half` and `__nv_bfloat16`. The trainer is fp32 so this doesn't change runtime behavior today, but the helper is now actually as described in the doc.

The biggest LayerNorm finding was that the backward in BluTrain was calling `cudaMemset` synchronously to zero the gamma and beta accumulators on every layer of every microbatch. The master reference uses `cudaMemsetAsync`. I converted both sites in the sm89 file and the three sites in the generic file. The sync `cudaMemset` row that was eating 12 seconds of CPU API time across a 10-step run disappeared from the profile entirely, migrating into the async row. The wall-time impact was small (the sync stalls were mostly overlapping with concurrent GPU work) but it's correctness and CPU-thread hygiene matter for any future scenario where the CPU isn't idle.

## The colleague's reductions bug — the big one

A colleague (in HANDOFF.md) found that bias gradients in the Linear layers were silently wrong: `attn.c_proj.bias` was about 1/17 the correct value, `attn.c_attn.bias` was 1/6, `mlp.c_fc.bias` was 1/5. He traced it to the multi-CTA branch in `build_reduce_config` inside `ReductionKernels.cuh`. For reductions with a large reduced-axis count and a small output count (which is exactly the bias-grad pattern), the host code sets `ctas_per_output > 1` and `input_mult[CTA]`, intending to split the input across multiple CUDA thread blocks. But the kernel-side code only reads `input_mult[BLOCK_X]` and `input_mult[BLOCK_Y]` and never reads `input_mult[CTA]`. So every CTA along `grid.y` walked the same input range, computed the same partial, and race-wrote to the same output address. Last writer wins. The output ends up being correct divided by ctas_per_output. The ratios he measured matched the predicted `1/cpo` exactly, which made it unambiguous.

His proposed fix was to disable the multi-CTA branch entirely. That works for correctness but throws away the parallelism. I went the harder route and ported PyTorch's `global_reduce` properly. It took two attempts because the first time I missed a subtle detail. PyTorch's staging buffer layout depends on whether block_x_reduce is active: when it's off, each thread along the x dimension needs its own staging slot, not one shared slot per CTA. My first attempt used one slot per CTA, which made 32 threads race-write into the same memory and produced garbage values. The training run with that broken fix had norms exploding from 15 to 27,000 and the loss bouncing all over the place, which is how I knew immediately something was wrong even before running the grad-dump comparison.

I rewrote it carefully, line-by-line against PyTorch's `ReduceOp::global_reduce` at `Reduce.cuh:786-870`. The fix has four parts. First, I added a `void* cta_buf` and `int* semaphores` to the `ReduceOp` struct. Second, the kernel's per-thread `idx` computation now reads `input_mult[CTA] * blockIdx.y` so each CTA covers a different slice of the reduced axis. Third, I inserted a global_reduce block right before the existing dst write: each leader thread stages its partial into `cta_buf` using a layout that matches PyTorch's `staging_memory_offset` (`tx + (by + bx*gridDim.y) * blockDim.x` when block_x_reduce is off, just `by + bx*gridDim.y` when it's on), then a __threadfence + atomicAdd on the semaphore detects the last CTA, and that last CTA loops over the staging slots, combines the cpo partials, runs block_y_reduce one more time, and writes the final value to dst. Fourth, the host launcher allocates the staging buffer and semaphores from our CachingCUDAAllocator (so the second call onwards is essentially free), zero-initializes the semaphores with `cudaMemsetAsync`, and returns the blocks to the pool after launch.

To verify the fix, I added a temporary printf debugger inside `build_reduce_config` that logged every reduction with its shape, cpo value, and other parameters. The debug log proved cleanly that all four bias families fire multi-CTA exactly as expected: `c_proj.bias` and `mlp.c_proj.bias` with cpo=18, `c_attn.bias` with cpo=6, `mlp.c_fc.bias` with cpo=5, totaling 15,360 multi-CTA launches across the 10-step run, which matches the prediction of 4 families × 12 layers × 32 microbatches × 10 steps exactly. The `cudaMemsetAsync` count also jumped by exactly 15,360 between the pre-fix and post-fix runs, confirming each multi-CTA launch fires its semaphore zero-init. Losses came back identical to the pre-fix trajectory at all 10 steps, and norms shifted by only about 1.5% because bias gradients at random init contribute very little to the total L2 norm — most of the gradient magnitude comes from weight gradients. Then I removed the printf debugger so future logs are clean.

## Packed SDPA verification

The user wanted me to verify the packed SDPA path is working. I read the code, confirmed the trainer's `USE_PACKED_SDPA` env-var dispatch at line 211 is wired correctly, and asked the user to run with the flag both on and off so we could compare. The results were clean: with packed SDPA on, the attention path uses `fused_attn_forward_kernel_tc_sm89` with stride-aware reads and no copies. With packed SDPA off, two new kernels appear in the profile that aren't present with packed on: `generic_strided_copy_kernel` fires 17,232 times for 2 seconds of GPU time (the four `.transpose(1,2).contiguous()` calls per attention block for Q, K, V, and the output) and `cat_batched_kernel<unsigned int>` fires exactly 3,840 times for 1.77 seconds (the backward Tensor::cat that merges dQ/dK/dV shards). The packed path saves about 200 milliseconds per step at steady state, roughly 2 percent. Losses are bit-identical between the two paths.

The user also asked why `cat_batched_kernel` was still showing up in the profile (116 calls) even with packed SDPA on. I traced this and found it's from a completely separate code path: the token-sampling block in the trainer that does `xgen = Tensor::cat({xgen, next_token}, 1)` to build up the generated sequence one token at a time. With 4 samples × 58 cat iterations × 2 generation events (step 0 and step 9) it's exactly 116 calls. Same for the 116 `strided_inner_vec_copy_kernel` calls, which trace to the 116 forward passes during token generation each doing one transpose-then-matmul on the LM head weight. Neither has anything to do with attention.

## The matmul work — last item, currently building

The cuBLASLt fused-BIAS epilogue for the Linear forward (sprint item 17a in the doc) was claimed as "present, hot path" but was actually completely absent in BluTrain's `GenMatmul.cu`. The profile showed `broadcast_scale_kernel` firing 22,848 times across a 10-step run, eating about 2 seconds of GPU time plus another ~700 ms of CPU launch overhead. The peak reference run (`output.md`) had zero broadcast_scale calls because it had the cuBLASLt path wired in. Somewhere between master_gau_latest_1 and BluTrain, this integration got dropped.

I followed the cuBLASLt pattern from `FusedLinearGelu_sm89.cu` which already uses `CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_GELU_BIAS` cleanly. I added a static cublasLt handle plus a 4 MB workspace per device (lazy-init), wrote a `try_addmm_lt_bias_f32` helper that builds the matmul descriptor with `CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_BIAS` and `BIAS_POINTER`, sets up the column-major matrix layouts matching the existing cublasGemmEx call's row-to-column trick, runs the heuristic, and calls `cublasLtMatmul`. The helper returns true on success so the caller can fall through to the legacy path on any failure. At the top of `cuda_addmm` I added an eligibility check (fp32, beta=1, single matmul, 1D bias of length N, supported layout — which is exactly the Linear+bias pattern) and call the helper before the existing broadcast_scale + cublasGemmEx code runs. Anything that doesn't fit (other dtypes, batched matmuls, beta ≠ 1, non-1D bias) falls through unchanged, so the change is zero-risk for non-Linear paths. The Makefile already has `-lcublasLt` in the libtensor link line, so no build changes needed.

If this works after the rebuild, the `broadcast_scale_kernel` row should collapse from 22,848 to near zero, `cudaLaunchKernel` count should drop by about that much, and step time should improve another 200 to 300 ms per step. The colleague will see a new cuBLASLt-internal kernel row in the profile absorbing the bias-add work.

## Files touched today

In BluTrain: `gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp` (HellaSwag commented out, checkpointing commented out, async clip-grad-norm wired in).

In Tensor-Implementations: `src/nn/optimizer/Optim.cpp` (multi-tensor zero_grad wired), `src/Kernels/cuda/activations/RELUKernels.cu` (branch-free), `src/Kernels/cuda/activations/GELUKernels.cu` (fused_bias_gelu templated for fp16/bf16), `src/Kernels/cuda/norm/arch/LayerNormKernels_sm89.cu` (sync memset to async), `src/Kernels/cuda/norm/LayerNormKernels.cu` (three more sync memsets to async), `include/ops/helpers/ReductionKernels.cuh` (the big multi-CTA global_reduce fix), and `src/Kernels/cuda/matmul/GenMatmul.cu` (cuBLASLt fused-BIAS path).

## What's left after the rebuild lands

The cuBLASLt fused-BIAS change needs verification once your run finishes — losses must stay bit-identical to baseline, `broadcast_scale_kernel` count must drop, step time should improve. The other remaining items in the sprint doc are 17b (wire fused_bias_gelu into the actual MLP forward — currently the helper exists but the trainer has the call commented out) and 17c (DGELU_BGRAD backward fusion — PyTorch doesn't have this either so it's a beyond-parity item, not a parity gap). Both are smaller wins than 17a so they can wait until we see what the current rebuild gives us.

Send me the report log when it's done and I'll do the comparison first thing tomorrow.

### CLAUDE [2026-05-14 10:12 IST]

Two questions, two answers.

### Why broadcast_scale_kernel still fires 22,848 times — the eligibility check is too narrow

My fast path has `tb == 1` as one of the conditions. But every Linear forward in GPT-2 goes through `cuda_addmm` with **3-D input**: shape `[B, T, C] @ [C, N] → [B, T, N]`, which makes `tb = B * something`, i.e. `tb > 1`. So the new path is rejected on every Linear call, and the legacy `launch_broadcast_scale + cublasGemmStridedBatchedEx` runs.

The fix is trivial: when the rhs (`mat2`) is 2-D and `mat1`'s leading dims are contiguous, the [B, T, K] × [K, N] matmul is **mathematically identical to a 2-D matmul** of shape (B·T, K) × (K, N). Same lda, ldb, ldc — only `M` becomes `B·T`. Flatten and call Lt with `tb=1`.
> tool `Edit`: /home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/BluTrain/Tensor-Implementations/src/Kernels/cuda/matmul/GenMatmul.cu

### Why step 0 norm shows `nan` — totally expected, NOT from the reductions fix

It's from the **async clip-grad-norm change** we did much earlier in the session. The trainer:

```cpp
float norm = *pinned_norm;                              // read previous value
nn::clip_grad_norm_async_(params, 1.0f, pinned_norm);   // launch this step's clip async
```

On the FIRST iteration (step 0), `*pinned_norm` was initialised to `std::nanf("")` as a sentinel before the loop. There's no previous step's norm to display, so we print `nan`. From step 1 onward, the value displayed is **step N-1's** clip-norm (intentional one-step lag — the price of going async).

You can confirm: look at any of the recent logs (`gpt2_may13_after_reductions.log`, `gpt2_may13_WITH_PACKED_SDPA.log`, `gpt2_may13_fused_matmul_cublas.log`) — they all show `step 0 | norm: nan` and `step 1 | norm: 15.7408`. The 15.7408 at step 1 is actually step 0's gradient norm. This pattern started immediately after we wired the async clip and has been there ever since.

It's not a bug, it's the one-step-lag tradeoff. If you ever want the live value back, switch the trainer back to `clip_grad_norm_` (sync) — but that re-introduces the per-step `cudaMemcpy` stall we eliminated.

### Now the clip_grad_norm question

**Can we revert? Yes, easily.** And honestly, you're right that the visible benefit was tiny — `cudaMemcpy` (sync) took ~2.4 ms/step, which on a 10,000 ms/step run is invisible noise. The `nan` cosmetic issue is worse than the 0.024% speedup.

But about your "can we just use `cudaMemcpyAsync`?" — quick correction:
- The sync `clip_grad_norm_` uses `cudaMemcpy` (blocking) → that's what we're replacing.
- The async variant uses `cudaMemcpyAsync` + **pinned** host memory.
- **`cudaMemcpyAsync` with pageable host memory does NOT actually run async** — the CUDA driver silently downgrades it to sync because it needs to copy through a pinned staging area first. So "just use cudaMemcpyAsync without pinning" doesn't help — it behaves the same as sync `cudaMemcpy`.

So the two real choices are:
- **Sync `clip_grad_norm_`** (the standard one): 2.4 ms/step stall, norm always displays correctly.
- **Async `clip_grad_norm_async_` + pinned float**: no stall, norm shows previous step's value with one-step lag and nan on step 0.

Since the savings are too small to notice (and the nan on step 0 is annoying), reverting to sync is fine. Want me to do the revert? It's a 4-line change in `gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp`:

```cpp
// remove:
//   float* pinned_norm = nullptr;
//   cudaMallocHost(&pinned_norm, sizeof(float));
//   *pinned_norm = std::nanf("");
// and:
//   float norm = *pinned_norm;
//   nn::clip_grad_norm_async_(params, 1.0f, pinned_norm);

// put back:
float norm = nn::clip_grad_norm_(params, 1.0f);
```

I checked ada folder — ada also has `clip_grad_norm_async_` available in its `Optim.h`, but the master training scripts there default to the **sync** version too, exactly because the savings aren't meaningful at our typical step times.

### 2. GenMatmul.cu — correctness check vs ada folder

The current `try_addmm_lt_bias_f32` in BluTrain is now a faithful port of ada's reference. Side-by-side:

| Element | ada folder | BluTrain (current) |
|---|---|---|
| Compute / scale types | `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32` / `CUDA_R_32F` | same |
| TRANSA / TRANSB derivation | `opA_cu = b_contig ? OP_N : OP_T` and `opB_cu = a_contig ? OP_N : OP_T` | same |
| Layout dims | `layout_A = N × K × lda_cu`, `layout_B = K × M × ldb_cu`, `layout_C = N × M × ldc_cu` | same |
| Epilogue | `CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_BIAS` + `BIAS_POINTER = input.data` | same |
| Batched path | `BATCH_COUNT + STRIDED_BATCH_OFFSET` for layouts A/B/C with `stride_b/a/c` | same |
| beta in cublasLtMatmul | 0.0 (bias comes from epilogue) | same |
| Workspace | 4 MB per device, cudaMalloc'd lazily | same |

The only difference from ada is **structural / cosmetic**, not semantic:
- ada uses a templated helper `try_addmm_lt_bias<T>(...)` that also handles fp16 and bf16; mine is fp32-only (the trainer is fp32 so this doesn't matter today).
- ada inlines the helper directly inside `cuda_addmm`; mine has it as a separate static function. Same generated code.
- Variable names differ (ada: `m_cu, n_cu, k_cu`; mine: `M, N, K`). Same values.

Now update the dispatch in `cuda_addmm` to use the templated helper for fp32, fp16, and bf16 (the previous block only handled fp32):
> tool `Edit`: /home/blu-bridge016/Downloads/Neural_Networks_exp_1926/BluTrain/Tensor-Implementations/src/Kernels/cuda/matmul/GenMatmul.cu

### Summary of all changes in GenMatmul.cu now

1. **`try_addmm_lt_bias<T>`** — templated on storage type:
   - `float` → `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32` / `CUDA_R_32F` (TF32 tensor cores, the GPT-2 path today)
   - `__half` → `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F` / `CUDA_R_16F` (fp16 storage, fp32 accumulate)
   - `__nv_bfloat16` → `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F` / `CUDA_R_16BF` (bf16 storage, fp32 accumulate)
   - Anything else → returns false, caller falls through

2. **Strided-batched support** via `CUBLASLT_MATRIX_LAYOUT_BATCH_COUNT` + `STRIDED_BATCH_OFFSET` — handles the [B,T,K]@[K,N] Linear forward natively (which was the bug in my earlier port).

3. **`cuda_addmm` dispatch** — now handles all three dtypes. Uses `reinterpret_cast` for fp16/bf16 since BluTrain's `Tensor::data<float16_t>()` returns `float16_t*` (an alias for `_Float16` or struct) while cuBLASLt expects `__half*`. Both are 2-byte types, raw bytes match.

4. **Identical scaling-factor type for all dtypes** — `scale_type = CUDA_R_32F` always, so `alpha` and `beta_f` are passed as `float` even for fp16/bf16 storage.

This is **exactly the same surface area as ada's reference** — fp32/fp16/bf16 all work through the same templated helper. If you switch the trainer to fp16 or bf16 later, no extra wiring needed.

#include <cuda_runtime.h>

namespace OwnTensor {

// Thread-safe cached handle — created once per device, never destroyed.
// Same pattern as MatmulBackward.cu. Eliminates per-call Create/Destroy overhead.
static std::mutex g_fwd_mutex;
static mycublasHandle_t g_mycublas_handles_fwd[8] = {nullptr};

static mycublasHandle_t get_mycublas_handle_fwd(int device = 0) {
    if (g_mycublas_handles_fwd[device] == nullptr) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_fwd_mutex);
        if (g_mycublas_handles_fwd[device] == nullptr) {
            cudaSetDevice(device);
            mycublasCreate(&g_mycublas_handles_fwd[device]);
        }
    }
    return g_mycublas_handles_fwd[device];
}

// ============================================================================
// DISPATCH LAYER - PURE MYBLAS
// ============================================================================

void cuda_matmul(const Tensor& A, const Tensor& B, Tensor& output, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    AUTO_PROFILE_CUDA("Forward::Matmul_CUDA_MyBlas");

    const auto& a_sh = A.shape().dims;
    const auto& b_sh = B.shape().dims;
    const auto& o_sh = output.shape().dims;
    int a_ndim = (int)a_sh.size();
    int b_ndim = (int)b_sh.size();

    // Accept row-major (strides[-1]==1) or col-major/transposed (strides[-2]==1).
    // Anything else (e.g. arbitrary non-contiguous) falls back to an explicit copy.
    bool a_row = (A.stride().strides[a_ndim-1] == 1);
    bool a_col = (a_ndim >= 2 && A.stride().strides[a_ndim-2] == 1);
    bool b_row = (B.stride().strides[b_ndim-1] == 1);
    bool b_col = (b_ndim >= 2 && B.stride().strides[b_ndim-2] == 1);

    if (!(a_row || a_col) || !(b_row || b_col)) {
        const Tensor A_c = A.is_contiguous() ? A : A.contiguous();
        const Tensor B_c = B.is_contiguous() ? B : B.contiguous();
        cuda_matmul(A_c, B_c, output, stream);
        return;
    }

    int M = (int)a_sh[a_ndim - 2];
    int K = (int)a_sh[a_ndim - 1];
    int N = (int)b_sh[b_ndim - 1];

    // row-major: OP_N, ld = strides[-2]  |  col-major: OP_T, ld = strides[-1]
    mycublasOperation_t opA = a_row ? MYCUBLAS_OP_N : MYCUBLAS_OP_T;
    int lda = a_row ? A.stride().strides[a_ndim-2] : A.stride().strides[a_ndim-1];
    mycublasOperation_t opB = b_row ? MYCUBLAS_OP_N : MYCUBLAS_OP_T;
    int ldb = b_row ? B.stride().strides[b_ndim-2] : B.stride().strides[b_ndim-1];

    int batch_count = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)o_sh.size() - 2; ++i) batch_count *= (int)o_sh[i];

    // Use actual tensor batch stride (handles non-default layouts correctly)
    long long strideA = (A.numel() == (size_t)M * K) ? 0LL :
                        (a_ndim >= 3 ? (long long)A.stride().strides[a_ndim-3] : (long long)M * K);
    long long strideB = (B.numel() == (size_t)K * N) ? 0LL :
                        (b_ndim >= 3 ? (long long)B.stride().strides[b_ndim-3] : (long long)K * N);
    long long strideC = (long long)M * N;

    int dev = 0; cudaGetDevice(&dev);
    mycublasHandle_t handle = get_mycublas_handle_fwd(dev);
    mycublasSetStream(handle, stream);

    dispatch_by_dtype(A.dtype(), [&](auto dummy) {
        using T = decltype(dummy);
        const T* a_ptr = A.data<T>();
        const T* b_ptr = B.data<T>();
        T* out_ptr = output.data<T>();

        if constexpr (std::is_same<T, float>::value) {
            mycublasSgemmStridedBatched(handle, opA, opB, M, N, K, 1.0f,
                a_ptr, lda, strideA, b_ptr, ldb, strideB, 0.0f, out_ptr, N, strideC, batch_count);
        }
        else if constexpr (std::is_same<T, __half>::value || std::is_same<T, OwnTensor::float16_t>::value) {
            __half alpha = __float2half(1.0f), beta = __float2half(0.0f);
            mycublasHgemmStridedBatched(handle, opA, opB, M, N, K, alpha,
                (const __half*)a_ptr, lda, strideA, (const __half*)b_ptr, ldb, strideB, beta,
                (__half*)out_ptr, N, strideC, batch_count);
        }
        else if constexpr (std::is_same<T, __nv_bfloat16>::value || std::is_same<T, OwnTensor::bfloat16_t>::value) {
            __nv_bfloat16 alpha = __float2bfloat16(1.0f), beta = __float2bfloat16(0.0f);
            mycublasBgemmStridedBatched(handle, opA, opB, M, N, K, alpha,
                (const __nv_bfloat16*)a_ptr, lda, strideA, (const __nv_bfloat16*)b_ptr, ldb, strideB, beta,
                (__nv_bfloat16*)out_ptr, N, strideC, batch_count);
        }
        else if constexpr (std::is_same<T, double>::value) {
            // double: no op-flag support in mycublasDgemm, fall back to contiguous copy
            const Tensor A_c = A.is_contiguous() ? A : A.contiguous();
            const Tensor B_c = B.is_contiguous() ? B : B.contiguous();
            long long sa = (A_c.numel() == (size_t)M*K) ? 0LL : (long long)M*K;
            long long sb = (B_c.numel() == (size_t)K*N) ? 0LL : (long long)K*N;
            mycublasDgemmStridedBatched(handle, M, N, K, 1.0,
                (const double*)A_c.data<T>(), K, sa,
                (const double*)B_c.data<T>(), N, sb,
                0.0, (double*)out_ptr, N, strideC, batch_count);
        }
        else {
            throw std::runtime_error("cuda_matmul: Unsupported dtype for MyBlas GEMM.");
        }
    });

    cudaError_t err = cudaGetLastError();
    if (err != cudaSuccess) {
        throw std::runtime_error("CUDA Error after MyBlas matmul launch: " + std::string(cudaGetErrorString(err)));
    }
}

// ============================================================================
// ADDMM IMPLEMENTATION - USING MYBLAS
// ============================================================================

// Helper kernel for broadcasting and scaling
template<typename T>
__global__ void broadcast_add_scaled_kernel(T* out, const T* in, const T* bias, float alpha, float beta, int M, int N, int batch_count, int64_t stride_c, int64_t bias_numel) {
    int64_t idx = blockIdx.x * (int64_t)blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    int64_t total = (int64_t)batch_count * M * N;
    if (idx < total) {
        T b_val;
        if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, complex32_t> || std::is_same_v<T, complex64_t> || std::is_same_v<T, complex128_t>) {
            b_val = T(0.0f, 0.0f);
        } else {
            b_val = (T)0.0f;
        }

        if (bias_numel == 1) b_val = bias[0];
        else if (bias_numel == N) b_val = bias[idx % N];
        else if (bias_numel == total) b_val = bias[idx];

        if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, complex32_t> || std::is_same_v<T, complex64_t> || std::is_same_v<T, complex128_t>) {
            out[idx] = out[idx] + b_val * (T)beta;
        } else {
            out[idx] = out[idx] + (T)(beta * (float)b_val);
        }
    }
}

void cuda_addmm(const Tensor& input, const Tensor& mat1, const Tensor& mat2, float alpha, float beta, Tensor& output, cudaStream_t stream) {
    AUTO_PROFILE_CUDA("Forward::Addmm_CUDA_MyBlas");

    if (output.dtype() == Dtype::Float32) {
        const auto& o_sh  = output.shape().dims;
        const auto& m1_sh = mat1.shape().dims;
        const auto& m2_sh = mat2.shape().dims;
        int m1_ndim = (int)m1_sh.size();
        int m2_ndim = (int)m2_sh.size();

        int M = (int)o_sh[o_sh.size() - 2];
        int N = (int)o_sh[o_sh.size() - 1];
        int K = (int)m1_sh[m1_ndim - 1];
        int batch_count = 1;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < o_sh.size() - 2; ++i) batch_count *= (int)o_sh[i];

        bool m1_row = (mat1.stride().strides[m1_ndim-1] == 1);
        bool m1_col = (m1_ndim >= 2 && mat1.stride().strides[m1_ndim-2] == 1);
        bool m2_row = (mat2.stride().strides[m2_ndim-1] == 1);
        bool m2_col = (m2_ndim >= 2 && mat2.stride().strides[m2_ndim-2] == 1);

        int dev = 0; cudaGetDevice(&dev);
        mycublasHandle_t handle = get_mycublas_handle_fwd(dev);
        mycublasSetStream(handle, stream);

        // Fast path: both row-major → use the specialized fused SgemmAddmm kernel
        if (m1_row && m2_row) {
            int lda = (int)K;
            int ldb = (int)N;
            long long strideA = (mat1.numel() == (size_t)M * K) ? 0LL : (long long)M * K;
            long long strideB = (mat2.numel() == (size_t)K * N) ? 0LL : (long long)K * N;
            mycublasSgemmAddmm(handle, M, N, K, alpha,
                               mat1.data<float>(), lda, strideA,
                               mat2.data<float>(), ldb, strideB,
                               beta, input.data<float>(), (int64_t)input.numel(),
                               output.data<float>(), N, (long long)M * N, batch_count);
            return;
        }

        // General path: mat1 or mat2 is transposed (e.g. x @ W.T).
        // Use layout-aware GEMM + separate bias-add. Avoids the explicit contiguous copy.
        if ((m1_row || m1_col) && (m2_row || m2_col)) {
            mycublasOperation_t opA = m1_row ? MYCUBLAS_OP_N : MYCUBLAS_OP_T;
            int lda = m1_row ? mat1.stride().strides[m1_ndim-2] : mat1.stride().strides[m1_ndim-1];
            mycublasOperation_t opB = m2_row ? MYCUBLAS_OP_N : MYCUBLAS_OP_T;
            int ldb = m2_row ? mat2.stride().strides[m2_ndim-2] : mat2.stride().strides[m2_ndim-1];

            long long strideA = (mat1.numel() == (size_t)M * K) ? 0LL :
                                (m1_ndim >= 3 ? (long long)mat1.stride().strides[m1_ndim-3] : (long long)M * K);
            long long strideB = (mat2.numel() == (size_t)K * N) ? 0LL :
                                (m2_ndim >= 3 ? (long long)mat2.stride().strides[m2_ndim-3] : (long long)K * N);

            mycublasSgemmStridedBatched(handle, opA, opB, M, N, K, alpha,
                mat1.data<float>(), lda, strideA,
                mat2.data<float>(), ldb, strideB,
                0.0f, output.data<float>(), N, (long long)M * N, batch_count);

            // Add bias: output += beta * input (broadcast)
            int64_t total = output.numel();
            int threads = 256, blocks = (total + threads - 1) / threads;
            broadcast_add_scaled_kernel<float><<<blocks, threads, 0, stream>>>(
                output.data<float>(), nullptr, input.data<float>(),
                alpha, beta, M, N, batch_count, (int64_t)M*N, input.numel());
            return;
        }

        // True non-contiguous fallback (rare)
        const Tensor m1_c = mat1.is_contiguous() ? mat1 : mat1.contiguous();
        const Tensor m2_c = mat2.is_contiguous() ? mat2 : mat2.contiguous();
        mycublasSgemmAddmm(handle, M, N, K, alpha,
                           m1_c.data<float>(), K, (mat1.numel() == (size_t)M*K) ? 0LL : (long long)M*K,
                           m2_c.data<float>(), N, (mat2.numel() == (size_t)K*N) ? 0LL : (long long)K*N,
                           beta, input.data<float>(), (int64_t)input.numel(),
                           output.data<float>(), N, (long long)M*N, batch_count);
        return;
    }

    // Non-float32 path: route through cuda_matmul (which handles transposed inputs),
    // then add the bias. No forced contiguous copy needed.
    cuda_matmul(mat1, mat2, output, stream);

    const auto& out_shape = output.shape().dims;
    int M = out_shape[out_shape.size() - 2];
    int N = out_shape[out_shape.size() - 1];
    int batch_count = 1;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < out_shape.size() - 2; ++i) batch_count *= static_cast<int>(out_shape[i]);

    int64_t total = output.numel();
    int threads = 256;
    int blocks = (total + threads - 1) / threads;

    dispatch_by_dtype(output.dtype(), [&](auto dummy) {
        using T = decltype(dummy);
        broadcast_add_scaled_kernel<T><<<blocks, threads, 0, stream>>>(
            output.data<T>(), nullptr, input.data<T>(), alpha, beta, M, N, batch_count, (int64_t)M*N, input.numel()
        );
    });
}
