            } else if (k + Config::BK < K) {
                asm volatile("cp.async.wait_group %0;\n" :: "n"(Config::STAGES - 2));
                __syncthreads();
                rs = (rs + 1) % Config::STAGES;
                ws = (ws + 1) % Config::STAGES;
                #pragma unroll
                for (int i = 0; i < Config::MMA_M; i++) {
                    #pragma unroll
                    for (int j = 0; j < Config::MMA_N; j++) if (i == 0) load_frB(frB[0][j], 0, j, rs);
                    load_frA(frA[0][i], 0, i, rs);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    const int g_epi = lane / 4, t_epi = lane % 4;
    float* dC = C + (long long)batch * strideC;

    #pragma unroll
    for (int i = 0; i < Config::MMA_M; i++) {
        #pragma unroll
        for (int j = 0; j < Config::MMA_N; j++) {
            const int r0 = by * BM + wy * Config::WARP_TILE_M + i * 16 + g_epi;
            const int r8 = r0 + 8;
            const int c0 = bx * BN + wx * Config::WARP_TILE_N + j * 8 + t_epi * 2;
            const int c1 = c0 + 1;

            float b0 = 0.f, b1 = 0.f;
            if (bias) {
                if (bias_numel == 1) {
                    b0 = b1 = bias[0];
                } else if (bias_numel == (int64_t)N) {
                    if (c0 < N) b0 = bias[c0];
                    if (c1 < N) b1 = bias[c1];
                } else if (bias_numel == (int64_t)M * N) {
                    const float* pb = bias + (long long)(batch % M) * N + c0;
                    if (c0 < N) b0 = pb[0];
                    if (c1 < N) b1 = pb[1];
                }
            }

            // FMA-fused epilogue for cuBLAS-matching single-rounding behavior
            auto store = [&](int r, int c, float f, float b) __attribute__((always_inline)) {
                if (r >= M || c >= N) return;
                float* dst = &dC[(long long)r * ldc + c];
                float s = __fmaf_rn(alpha, f, 0.f);
                if (bias) {
                    *dst = __fmaf_rn(beta, b, s);
                } else {
                    *dst = (beta == 0.f) ? s : __fmaf_rn(beta, *dst, s);
                }
            };

            store(r0, c0, acc[i][j][0], b0);
            store(r0, c1, acc[i][j][1], b1);
            store(r8, c0, acc[i][j][2], b0);
            store(r8, c1, acc[i][j][3], b1);
        }
    }
}

template <int BM, int BN, int BK, int STAGES, int THREADS, bool IsAligned>
static void launch_sgemm_addmm_sm89(
    cudaStream_t stream, int M, int N, int K,
    float alpha,
    const float* A, int lda, long long strideA,
    const float* B, int ldb, long long strideB,
    float beta,
    const float* bias, int64_t bias_numel,
    float* C, int ldc, long long strideC,
    int batchCount)
{
    using Config = SgemmTileConfig<BM, BN, BK, STAGES, THREADS>;
    static const size_t smem_bytes = STAGES * Config::STAGE_SIZE * sizeof(float);

    static std::unordered_map<const void*, bool> done;
    const void* fn = (const void*)sgemm_addmm_sm89_kernel<BM, BN, BK, STAGES, THREADS, IsAligned>;
    if (!done[fn]) {
        cudaFuncSetAttribute(fn, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, (int)smem_bytes);
        done[fn] = true;
    }

    const int gx = (N + BN - 1) / BN, gy = (M + BM - 1) / BM;
    sgemm_addmm_sm89_kernel<BM, BN, BK, STAGES, THREADS, IsAligned>
        <<<dim3(gx, gy, batchCount), THREADS, smem_bytes, stream>>>(
            M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
            beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
}

template <int BM, int BN, int BK, int STAGES, int THREADS>
static void dispatch_sgemm_addmm_sm89(
    cudaStream_t stream, int M, int N, int K,
    float alpha,
    const float* A, int lda, long long strideA,
    const float* B, int ldb, long long strideB,
    float beta,
    const float* bias, int64_t bias_numel,
    float* C, int ldc, long long strideC,
    int batchCount)
{
    const bool aligned = (((size_t)A & 15) == 0) && (((size_t)B & 15) == 0)
                      && ((lda & 3) == 0) && ((ldb & 3) == 0);
    if (aligned)
        launch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<BM, BN, BK, STAGES, THREADS, true>(
            stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
            beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
    else
        launch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<BM, BN, BK, STAGES, THREADS, false>(
            stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
            beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
}

// Tile heuristic: 256x128 large, 128x128 mid (BK gated by K), 64x64 small
extern "C" void mycublasSgemmAddmm_sm89(
    mycublasHandle_t handle,
    int M, int N, int K,
    const float alpha,
    const float* A, int lda, long long int strideA,
    const float* B, int ldb, long long int strideB,
    const float beta,
    const float* bias, int64_t bias_numel,
    float* C, int ldc, long long int strideC,
    int batchCount)
{
    cudaStream_t stream = handle ? handle->stream : 0;

    if (M >= 256 && N >= 128) {
        dispatch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<256, 128, 32, 2, 256>(
            stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
            beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
    } else if (M >= 128 && N >= 128) {
        if (K >= 256) {
            dispatch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<128, 128, 32, 3, 128>(
                stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
                beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
        } else {
            dispatch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<128, 128, 16, 6, 128>(
                stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
                beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
        }
    } else {
        // edits: Gautam_Reddy_1926 — H1 (THREADS=128) + H2 (ldmatrix), STAGES=6 kept (S=10 regressed due to occupancy cliff)
        dispatch_sgemm_addmm_sm89<64, 64, 16, 6, 128>(
            stream, M, N, K, alpha, A, lda, strideA, B, ldb, strideB,
            beta, bias, bias_numel, C, ldc, strideC, batchCount);
    }
}

deep research done bro

**root cause of the #3 TN kernel being 4× slower:**

read the templated kernel [Sgemm_core_template_sm89.cuh](BluTrain_best_precision/Tensor-Implementations/BluBridge-BLAS/src/level3/batched_gemm/FP32/SM89/Sgemm_core_template_sm89.cuh) which serves all 3 layouts (NT, TN, NN). key finding:

**the specialized NT 256x128 kernel ([Sgemm_nt_256x128_sm89.cu](BluTrain_best_precision/Tensor-Implementations/BluBridge-BLAS/src/level3/batched_gemm/FP32/SM89/Sgemm_nt_256x128_sm89.cu)) uses LDSM_X4 for A** (line 128). but **the templated kernel that serves TN uses MANUAL 4 reads** (line 212-213) — no ldmatrix.

so:
- NT bwd dX → fast specialized kernel WITH ldmatrix → 768µs/call
- TN bwd dW → templated kernel WITHOUT ldmatrix → 3039µs/call (4× slower)
- 8000 calls × (3039 - 768) µs = ~18 sec recoverable IF we could close the gap

**but TN A is structurally hostile to ldmatrix:**

for TN, A is stored in smem as (K, M) — rows = K, cols = M, M is contiguous. but m16n8k8 needs A in (M, K) register layout. options:

1. **ldmatrix.trans**: would swap K↔M during load. BUT we already established `ldmatrix.trans` is broken for TF32 (b16-transpose puts halves of different TF32 values into one b32 register — silent NaN bug we hit last week)
2. **change TN smem layout** to (M, K) instead of (K, M): requires "transpose-during-write" from global → smem, which kills coalescing
3. **plain ldmatrix without trans**: reads M-contiguous 4 TF32 per lane, which is the WRONG axis (we want K-contiguous in registers)

**realistic options for #3:**

| approach | risk | est gain |
|---|---|---|
| (a) port B-side Congruous swizzle to TN kernel (we know this pattern works from 64x64) | medium | maybe 5-15% (B-side only) |
| (b) write a new dedicated TN 256x128 kernel modeled after NT specialized, with TN-specific tricks | high (multi-hour, multi-iteration) | possibly 2-3× |
| (c) tune STAGES (4 currently) and MMA schedule | low | likely noise |

honest read: this isn't a quick win like #1 was. it's structural. options (b) is the only path to closing the 4× gap, and it's a substantial project with NaN risk (like the last B-side ldmatrix.trans incident).

**what i recommend:**

skip #3 for now (too risky/long), do **#4 (add 256x64 dispatch)** which is dispatcher-only work, then **#5 (128x128 addmm)** which can reuse the same ldmatrix.x4 + Crosswise pattern that won on 64x64.

OR — if you really want to attack #3, we go option (a) first (B-side Congruous swizzle port from 64x64) as a smaller validated step before any A-side refactor.

> tool `Agent`: Cutlass TN TF32 m16n8k8 design research

definitive answer from research bro

**cutlass ALSO uses scalar loads for TF32 TN A — there's no clean ldmatrix solution.**

key facts verified from cutlass source:
1. **NT TF32 A** → uses `TensorOpMultiplicandCrosswise` layout → **ldmatrix.x4** at [mma_tensor_op_tile_iterator.h:2621](cutlass/include/cutlass/gemm/warp/mma_tensor_op_tile_iterator.h#L2621) ✓
2. **TN TF32 A** → uses `ColumnMajorTensorOpMultiplicandCongruous` wrapper → which delegates to base `TensorOpMultiplicandCongruous<32,32>` → **scalar loads** at line 771-772 (same path as B operand)
3. cutlass picks Congruous (not Crosswise) for TN because ldmatrix.trans on TF32 breaks (the NaN bug we hit)
4. **TF32 ldmatrix without trans doesn't work for TN because the b16-granularity doesn't align with TF32's 32-bit boundary on the transposed axis**

**so our TN kernel @ 3039µs IS actually near-optimal for this layout.** the original ranked list's claim "1.73× slower than CUTLASS" was a wrong comparison — they compared our TN kernel against cuBLAS's NT kernel (different orientation, not apples-to-apples).

**what cuBLAS likely does to win on bwd dW:**

bwd dW computes `dW = X.T @ dY`. mathematically: `dW = (dY.T @ X).T`. so instead of computing as TN (slow), reorient as NT (fast) and transpose the result.

- compute `dW.T = dY.T @ X` via NT path → uses ldmatrix → ~768µs
- transpose dW.T → dW (only 768×768 = 2.3MB) → ~50-100µs
- net: ~800-900µs per call vs current 3039µs
- savings: ~17 seconds across 8000 calls

**but this is NOT a BluBLAS change** — it requires the training loop / autograd code to reorient the bwd dW operation. that's outside the kernel layer.

**realistic conclusion for #3:**
- closing the TN kernel itself isn't possible without rewriting outside cutlass's design (NaN risk)
- the real win lives at the call-site (reorient bwd dW from TN to NT-then-transpose), which is a different scope of change
- inside BluBLAS, only marginal wins (~5-10%) possible on TN kernel via B-side Congruous swizzle and MMA reorder

**recommendation:** skip #3 (structural, needs call-site changes). move to #4 (256x64 dispatch) and #5 (128x128 addmm ldmatrix port) which are tractable kernel-level wins.

OR: if you want to chase the bwd dW win properly, the real fix is at the training loop level — reorient bwd dW to compute dW.T (NT) then transpose. that's a different codebase change.

## PART 4: ADDMM (fused matmul+bias) — how each handles it

**BluBLAS approach:** we have a dedicated `sgemm_addmm_sm89_kernel` family that fuses (alpha * A @ B + beta * bias) into ONE kernel call. variants:
- `addmm 64x64` for small-M (HellaSwag)
- `addmm 256x128` for training forward big
- `addmm 128x128` for mid-size

**cuBLAS approach:** does NOT have a fused addmm. it does:
1. pure gemm: `s1688gemm_*_nn_align4`
2. then a separate add kernel for bias (in nsys i can see `vectorized_kernel_impl<Add>` 493440 calls in BOTH runs — same count)

so cuBLAS pays 2 kernel launches per addmm op, we pay 1. fusion is OUR structural advantage. **yet they're still faster overall on the matmul portion.** meaning their raw gemm is fast enough to absorb the extra launch cost.

call-count proof: both runs have identical 493440 `Add` calls — so even our addmm runs DO trigger a bias add somewhere else, OR cuBLAS uses the Add kernel for non-bias purposes. either way, fusion isn't the structural moat we hoped.

**path 1 — BluBLAS** (line 2599, label `"Forward::Addmm_CUDA_MyBlas"`):

- one `cublasLtMatmul` call (line 2938) — **FUSED matmul + bias in single kernel**, exactly like ours

## STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES (the why behind the gap)

**(1) register pressure: cuBLAS uses 20-40 fewer regs/thread everywhere**

| role | BluBLAS regs | cuBLAS regs | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64x64 fwd small | 113 | 90 | -23 |
| 256x128 bwd dW | 255 (maxed) | 216 | -39 |
| 256x128 bwd dX | 236 | 222 | -14 |
| 256x128 NN fwd | 255 (maxed) | 224 | -31 |
| 128x128 mid | 255 (maxed) | 221/228 | -27 |

**we're hitting the 255-register cap on 5 kernels** — that means the compiler is spilling to local memory in places, hurting performance. cuBLAS stays in the ~215-228 range with headroom.

**(2) smem usage: cuBLAS uses less smem too**
- 256x128 family: cuBLAS 72 KB vs ours 96 KB (-25%)
- this matters because their `STAGES=3` vs our `STAGES=4` and `STAGES=2`
- with less smem they leave more L2 headroom

**(3) tile diversity: cuBLAS has 11 variants, we have 10**
- cuBLAS has the **256x64 nn/tn pair** (we don't have 256x64 at all)
- cuBLAS has **gemmSN_NN_kernel** for tiny gemv-like (we don't — we bash through bigger kernels)
- cuBLAS has **128x256 in all 3 orientations** (nt/tn/nn) — we only have 256x128
- cuBLAS uses **128x64 tn** for tiny bwd, where we go straight to 128x128 or 64x64

**(4) occupancy: nearly all 256x128 kernels are 1-block/SM in both libraries** — register-bound. so we can't gain from more occupancy on big tiles. the wins must come from per-instruction efficiency (lower regs, better ILP).

---

## WHERE EACH KERNEL WINS/LOSES (head-to-head per role)

| role | BluBLAS | cuBLAS | per-call gap | total gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fwd small-M (eval) 64x64 | 40.8µs | 25.9µs | **1.58× slower** | **+10,485 ms** |
| bwd dW 256x128 | 3050µs TN | 1694µs (they use 128x256 NT — flipped!) | **1.80× slower** | **+10,850 ms** |
| bwd dX 256x128 | 770µs × 30K calls | 1731µs × 5.9K calls | per-call 2.2× FASTER | **+12,790 ms** (fanout!) |
| fwd N=64 17K calls | 862µs (256x128 over-tiles) | 755µs (256x64 right-sized) | 1.14× slower | **+1,829 ms** |
| mid-mix 11K-99K calls | 98.5µs spread across 1 tile | 628µs spread across 6 variants | per-call we WIN but volume mismatch | **+2,807 ms** |
| lm_head NN | 19,994µs | 17,669µs | 1.13× slower | **+744 ms** |
| bwd medium 7.6K | 908µs + 16µs scale | 596µs + 513µs (two variants) | spread WINS for us | **-1,541 ms** |

## CONCRETE TAKEAWAYS

1. **64x64 is 28.9% of matmul time in BOTH libraries** — biggest hotspot. our 113 regs vs their 90 regs is the key delta. need ncu to see if we have spills or stall reasons.

2. **256x128 is register-maxed in BluBLAS** (255/thread). compiler can't be more conservative. likely we have spills. cuBLAS's 216-228 range = no spills, full ILP. major source of per-call gap.

3. **bwd dX fanout: 30,894 vs 5,914 calls** — this is the SINGLE biggest gap (+12.8s) and it's purely call count. cuBLAS handles the same workload in 5× fewer launches. they likely use bigger tiles for some shape we route to 256x128. dispatcher fix.

4. **bwd dW flip trick**: cuBLAS computes the same logical matmul as **128x256 NT** instead of **256x128 TN** — escape route from the TF32 TN structural problem. they do this at dispatch time.

5. **missing tiles**: 256x64 (saves 1.8s), 128x256 nt/nn (would help bwd dW), gemmSN-like (32 ms, tiny).

## inefficiencies found in eval/HellaSwag/gen code

### 1. HellaSwag ([hellaswag_eval.h:103-116](BluTrain_best_precision/hellaswag_eval.h#L103-L116)) — 4 problems
```cpp
for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r) {
    Tensor lg = logits.narrow_view(0, r, 1)
                      .narrow_view(1, ex.ctx_len - 1, end_len)
                      .contiguous();  // ❌ alloc + copy kernel per candidate
    Tensor tg = toks_dev.narrow_view(0, r, 1)
                        .narrow_view(1, ex.ctx_len, end_len)
                        .contiguous();  // ❌ alloc + copy kernel per candidate
    Tensor loss = autograd::sparse_cross_entropy_loss(lg, tg);
    losses[r] = loss.to_cpu().data<float>()[0];  // ❌ D2H sync per candidate
}
```

- **4× `to_cpu()` per example** → **40,168 D2H syncs total** for 10K examples × 4 candidates. each sync stalls the GPU pipeline
- **`contiguous()` on narrow_view** allocates fresh tensor + copy kernel per candidate per example = ~80K extra allocations + copies
- **per-example H2D copy** of token tensor (line 92-94) = 10K H2D transfers
- **per-example separate forward pass** with M=4 → routes to the slow 64x64 kernel × 10K times. could batch many small examples together but variable max_len makes it tricky

### 2. token generation ([gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:1173-1249](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L1173-L1249)) — 3 problems

```cpp
while (xgen.shape().dims[1] < max_length) {
    Tensor logits = model.forward(xgen);  // ❌ no KV cache - re-processes WHOLE sequence
    ...
    Tensor logits_cpu = last_logits_3d.to_cpu();  // ❌ D2H per token
    for (int64_t b = 0; b < B; ++b) {
        std::partial_sort(idx.begin(), idx.begin()+TOPK, idx.end(), ...);  // ❌ CPU top-k over V=50304
        ...
    }
    xgen = Tensor::cat({xgen, next_token}, 1);  // ❌ re-allocates per token
}
```

- **no KV cache** — every token regenerates the entire sequence from scratch. token at position 30 runs forward on length-30 input even though only 1 token is new. quadratic cost
- **CPU-side top-k + softmax** — the code comment says "fused CUDA softmax kernel occasionally produces NaN" so they fell back to CPU. that means D2H + CPU work per token + back. could be fixed at the kernel level
- **`Tensor::cat` per token** — re-allocates the growing sequence tensor each iteration

**pytorch** ([gpt2.py:632-651](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2.py#L632-L651)):

**ours** ([gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:1106-1124](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L1106-L1124)):
```cpp

    Tensor logits = model.forward(batch.input);
    Tensor loss = sparse_cross_entropy_loss(logits, batch.target);
    Tensor loss_cpu = loss.to_cpu();  // ❌ D2H sync EVERY val_step (20 syncs)
    val_loss_accum += loss_cpu.data<float>()[0] / 20.0f;

```

**math:** same ✓ — both average 20 batches of cross-entropy
**efficiency:** ours does **20 D2H syncs** vs pytorch's **1**. each sync stalls the GPU. **inefficient but correct.**

## HELLASWAG — implementation comparison

**pytorch** ([gpt2.py:258-275](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2.py#L258-L275) — `get_most_likely_row`):
```python
def get_most_likely_row(tokens, mask, logits):
    shift_logits = logits[..., :-1, :].contiguous()
    shift_tokens = tokens[..., 1:].contiguous()
    flat_shift_logits = shift_logits.view(-1, V)
    flat_shift_tokens = shift_tokens.view(-1)
    shift_losses = F.cross_entropy(flat_shift_logits, flat_shift_tokens, reduction='none')  # ✓ ONE call for all 4 rows
    shift_losses = shift_losses.view(4, -1)
    shift_mask = mask[..., 1:].contiguous()
    masked_shift_losses = shift_losses * shift_mask  # ✓ mask-based selection
    avg_loss = masked_shift_losses.sum(dim=1) / shift_mask.sum(dim=1)
    pred_norm = avg_loss.argmin().item()  # ✓ ONE D2H sync per example
    return pred_norm
```

**ours** ([hellaswag_eval.h:103-122](BluTrain_best_precision/hellaswag_eval.h#L103-L122)):
```cpp
float losses[4];
for (int r = 0; r < 4; ++r) {  // ❌ loop over 4 rows separately
    Tensor lg = logits.narrow_view(0,r,1).narrow_view(1,ctx-1,end_len).contiguous();  // ❌ alloc+copy
    Tensor tg = toks_dev.narrow_view(0,r,1).narrow_view(1,ctx,end_len).contiguous();   // ❌ alloc+copy
    Tensor loss = sparse_cross_entropy_loss(lg, tg);  // ❌ 4 separate CE kernel launches
    losses[r] = loss.to_cpu().data<float>()[0];  // ❌ 4 D2H syncs per example
}
// CPU argmin over losses[4]
```

**math:** equivalent ✓
- pytorch: computes loss at ALL positions, then mask out non-completion positions → same result as ours
- ours: slices completion span via narrow_view then computes loss only on that span
- **both produce identical numbers** — our HellaSwag accuracy 2565/2559 matches expected

**efficiency:** 
| operation | pytorch | ours | factor |
|---|---|---|---|
| cross_entropy calls per example | 1 | 4 | **4× more launches** |
| D2H syncs per example | 1 | 4 | **4× more syncs** |
| `.contiguous()` alloc/copy ops | 2 | 8 | **4× more allocations** |
| total syncs (10042 ex) | 10,042 | 40,168 | **+30K extra syncs** |

## TOKEN GENERATION — implementation comparison

**pytorch** ([gpt2.py:705-733](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2.py#L705-L733)):
```python
while xgen.size(1) < max_length:
    logits, _ = model(xgen)
    logits = logits[:, -1, :]
    probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)            # ✓ GPU softmax
    topk_probs, topk_indices = torch.topk(probs, 50, dim=-1)  # ✓ GPU topk
    ix = torch.multinomial(topk_probs, 1, generator=sample_rng)  # ✓ GPU multinomial
    xcol = torch.gather(topk_indices, -1, ix)    # ✓ GPU gather
    xgen = torch.cat((xgen, xcol), dim=1)
# decode at the end
```

**ours** ([gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp:1185-1248](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L1185-L1248)):
```cpp
while (xgen.shape().dims[1] < max_length) {
    Tensor logits = model.forward(xgen);
    Tensor last_logits_3d = logits.narrow_view(1, T-1, 1).contiguous();
    Tensor logits_cpu = last_logits_3d.to_cpu();  // ❌ D2H FULL [B,V] floats per token
    // CPU partial_sort over V=50304 — ❌ huge CPU work per token per batch
    // CPU exp, sum, sample — ❌ done on CPU due to "softmax kernel NaN bug"
    Tensor next_token = next_token_cpu.to(device);  // ❌ H2D back
    xgen = Tensor::cat({xgen, next_token}, 1);
}
```

the code comment at [line 1200-1203](BluTrain_best_precision/gpt2_fmha_ddp.cpp#L1200-L1203) explains:
> "The fused CUDA softmax kernel (SoftmaxKernels.cu) occasionally produces NaN for one row; since generation is cheap (B*V floats per step), we do top-k + softmax on the CPU directly from logits. This sidesteps the kernel bug entirely."

**math:** same ✓ — both do top-50 softmax sampling with multinomial
**efficiency:** ours is MUCH worse:
- D2H of [B,V] floats per token = 4 × 50304 × 4 bytes = 800KB transfer × 240 tokens
- CPU partial_sort over 50K elements × 4 batches × 240 tokens = millions of comparisons
- H2D of next token back per step
- pytorch keeps everything on GPU until end

with eval/gen stripped, the timeline should look like:
- step 0: val_loss only → ~10-15 sec (val takes some time but no HellaSwag/gen)
- steps 1-8: pure training ~10.5 sec each
- step 9: val_loss only → ~10-15 sec
- total: ~110-130 sec for 10 steps (down from 170/162 sec)

the gap between BluBLAS and cuBLAS should now be **just the training throughput gap** = ~3-4 sec across 10 steps = **3-4% slower**. that's the real engineering target.

// Runtime toggle: when true, Attention::forward uses the packed-QKV fused
// SDPA path (scaled_dot_product_attention_packed) — skipping shard,
// reshape+transpose of Q/K/V on the way in, and transpose+reshape of the
// merged output on the way out. When false, the original unfused path is
// used. Set by the USE_PACKED_SDPA env var in main().
static bool g_use_packed_sdpa = false;

// Runtime toggle for the unfused path only: when true, reshape qkv to
// [B,T,H,3*d] (free view on contiguous qkv) and then shard axis 3 — avoids
// the 3 contiguous copies that the original shard-axis-2 → reshape route
// forces. Ignored when g_use_packed_sdpa is true. Set by USE_QKV_RESHAPE_FIRST.
static bool g_use_qkv_reshape_first = false;

struct GPTConfig {
    int64_t context_length = 1024;
    int64_t vocab_size = 50304;  // GPT-2 vocab size
    int64_t n_embd = 768;
    int64_t n_layers = 12;
    int64_t n_heads = 12;       // GPT-2 124M
    bool weight_tying = true;     // Flag for weight tying
    bool checkpointing = false;
    bool if_log = true;
};

// =============================================================================
// Single shared advancing RNG (mirrors gpt2.py's torch.manual_seed(1234) +
// apply(_init_weights) — one stream advanced across every parameter draw).
// =============================================================================
//
// Tensor::randn(shape, opts, seed, std) constructs a fresh std::mt19937 / cuRAND
// state on each call, so its per-call seed cannot share state across draws.
// Bypass it for parameter init: draw all init values from one std::mt19937 here
// and copy_ each draw into the parameter (CPU→device handled by copy_, which is
// already how init_linear_gpt2 worked). LayerNorms are not touched (gpt2.py's
// _init_weights doesn't either — they keep the default weight=1, bias=0).
//
// Advancement order matches PyTorch's apply(_init_weights) traversal:
//   wte → wpe → for each block: (c_attn, attn.c_proj, mlp.c_fc, mlp.c_proj)
//        → lm_head    (overwrites wte when weight_tying=true)

struct InitRng {
    std::mt19937 gen;
    explicit InitRng(uint64_t seed) : gen(static_cast<uint32_t>(seed)) {}

    // CPU float32 tensor drawn from N(0, std) using the shared advancing stream.
    Tensor normal(const Shape& shape, float std) {
        Tensor t(shape, TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Float32));
        std::normal_distribution<float> dist(0.0f, std);
        float* data = t.data<float>();
        size_t n = t.numel();
        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) data[i] = dist(gen);
        return t;
    }
};

// =============================================================================
// Embedding Layer with Autograd Support
// =============================================================================

class Embedding : public nn::Module {
public:
    Tensor weight;  // [vocab_size, n_embd]
    std::string name;  // canonical module path for PrecLogger (e.g. "wte")
    Embedding() = default;
    Embedding(int64_t vocab_size, int64_t embed_dim, DeviceIndex device, InitRng& rng,
              std::string nm = {})
        : name(std::move(nm)), vocab_size_(vocab_size), embed_dim_(embed_dim)
    {
        // Allocate the parameter on device WITHOUT req_grad first, fill it via
        // copy_ from a CPU draw on the shared RNG stream, THEN flip on req_grad
        // — matches init_linear_gpt2's order so copy_ never runs against a
        // leaf with grad-tracking already enabled. Done this way (rather than
        // constructing via Tensor::randn) so a single std::mt19937 advances
        // across every parameter init in the model.
        TensorOptions opts = TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Float32)
                                          .with_device(device);
        weight = Tensor(Shape{{vocab_size, embed_dim}}, opts);
        Tensor init_data = rng.normal(Shape{{vocab_size, embed_dim}}, 0.02f);
        weight.copy_(init_data);
        weight.set_requires_grad(true);

        register_parameter(weight);
    }
    
    // Forward: indices [B, T] -> embeddings [B, T, C]
    Tensor forward(const Tensor& indices) override {
        Tensor out = autograd::embedding(weight, indices);
        // No fwd_in dump: indices are Int64 (logger skips non-float32 anyway).
        PREC_DUMP(name, "fwd_out", out);
        return out;
    }
    
private:
    int64_t vocab_size_;
    int64_t embed_dim_;
};

// =============================================================================
// Helper: Initialize nn::Linear weights with GPT-2 style (std=0.02)
// =============================================================================

void init_linear_gpt2(nn::Linear& layer, float std, InitRng& rng, bool req_grad=true) {
    // IMPORTANT: Do NOT replace layer.weight with a new tensor!
    // nn::Linear already registered its weight in params_.
    // We must copy data INTO the existing weight to preserve parameter identity.
    Tensor init_data = rng.normal(layer.weight.shape(), std);
    layer.weight.copy_(init_data);
    layer.weight.set_requires_grad(req_grad);

    if (layer.bias.is_valid()) {
        Tensor bias_init = Tensor::zeros(layer.bias.shape(),
                                         TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Float32));
        layer.bias.copy_(bias_init);
        layer.bias.set_requires_grad(req_grad);
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Multi-Head Causal Self-Attention (FIXED)
// =============================================================================

class Attention : public nn::Module {
public:
    nn::LayerNorm ln;        // Pre-norm LayerNorm
    nn::Linear c_attn;       // QKV projection: [n_embd] -> [3 * n_embd]
    nn::Linear c_proj;       // Output projection: [n_embd] -> [n_embd]
    
    std::string name;  // canonical path prefix, e.g. "h.0.attn"
    Attention(int64_t n_embd, int n_heads, int n_layers, DeviceIndex device, InitRng& rng,
              std::string nm = {})
        : name(std::move(nm)),
          ln(n_embd),
          c_attn(n_embd, 3 * n_embd, true),
          c_proj(n_embd, n_embd, true),
          n_embd_(n_embd),
          n_heads_(n_heads),
          head_dim_(n_embd / n_heads)
    {
        // GPT-2 style init for qkv projection
        init_linear_gpt2(c_attn, 0.02f, rng);
        
        // Scaled init for residual projection: std *= (2 * n_layers) ** -0.5
        float scale = 1.0f / std::sqrt(2.0f * static_cast<float>(n_layers));
        init_linear_gpt2(c_proj, 0.02f * scale, rng);

        // Pre-compute attention scale on GPU once
        scale_ = Tensor::full(Shape{{1}}, TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Float32).with_device(device),
                              1.0f / std::sqrt(static_cast<float>(head_dim_)));

        ln.to(device);
        c_attn.to(device);
        c_proj.to(device);

        register_module(ln);
        register_module(c_attn);
        register_module(c_proj);
    }

    Tensor forward(const Tensor& x) override {
        int64_t B = x.shape().dims[0];
        int64_t T = x.shape().dims[1];
        int64_t C = x.shape().dims[2];

        PREC_DUMP(name, "fwd_in", x);

        // Pre-Norm
        Tensor h = ln.forward(x);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".ln_1", x, h);

        // QKV Projection
        Tensor qkv = c_attn.forward(h);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".c_attn", h, qkv);

        // Two paths, gated by USE_PACKED_SDPA env var (read once at startup):
        //   USE_PACKED_SDPA=1  → packed: zero shard / reshape / transpose / cat
        //   USE_PACKED_SDPA=0  → original shard-axis-2 path (relies on smart
        //                        reshape + stride-aware kernels for partial fix)
        static const bool kUsePackedSdpa = []() {
            const char* e = std::getenv("USE_PACKED_SDPA");
            return e && e[0] == '1';
        }();

        Tensor merged;
        if (kUsePackedSdpa) {
            merged = autograd::scaled_dot_product_attention_packed(
                qkv, n_heads_, /*is_causal=*/true, /*dropout_p=*/0.0f,
                autograd::SDPBackend::MemoryEfficient);
        } else {
            std::vector<Tensor> inp = qkv.make_shards_inplace_axis(3, 2);
            Tensor q = inp[0];
            Tensor k = inp[1];
            Tensor v = inp[2];

            q = autograd::transpose( autograd::reshape(q, Shape({{B, T, n_heads_, head_dim_}})), 1, 2);
            k = autograd::transpose( autograd::reshape(k, Shape({{B, T, n_heads_, head_dim_}})), 1, 2);
            v = autograd::transpose( autograd::reshape(v, Shape({{B, T, n_heads_, head_dim_}})), 1, 2);

            Tensor attn_out = autograd::scaled_dot_product_attention(
                    q, k, v, /*is_causal=*/true, 0.0f, autograd::SDPBackend::MemoryEfficient);

            merged = autograd::reshape(
                                autograd::transpose(attn_out, 1, 2),
                                Shape({{B, T, C}}));
        }

        PREC_DUMP(name + ".sdpa", "fwd_out", merged);

        Tensor proj = c_proj.forward(merged);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".c_proj", merged, proj);

        // Residual connection
        Tensor out = autograd::add(x, proj);
        PREC_DUMP(name, "fwd_out", out);
        return out;
    }
    
private:
    int64_t n_embd_;
    int64_t n_heads_;
    int64_t head_dim_;
    Tensor scale_;  // Pre-computed 1/sqrt(head_dim), reused across forward calls
};


// =============================================================================
// MLP Block
// =============================================================================

class MLP : public nn::Module {
public:
    nn::LayerNorm ln;       // LayerNorm before MLP
    nn::Linear fc_up;       // Linear(n_embd, 4*n_embd)
    nn::Linear fc_down;     // Linear(4*n_embd, n_embd)
    
    std::string name;  // canonical path prefix, e.g. "h.0.mlp"
    MLP(int64_t n_embd, int n_layers, DeviceIndex device, InitRng& rng,
        std::string nm = {})
        : name(std::move(nm)),
          ln(n_embd),
          fc_up(n_embd, 4 * n_embd, true),
          fc_down(4 * n_embd, n_embd, true),
          n_embd_(n_embd)
    {
        // Init order matches gpt2.py MLP.apply(_init_weights):
        //   c_fc / fc_up   (std=0.02), then
        //   c_proj/fc_down (std=0.02 * (2L)^-0.5 — NANOGPT_SCALE_INIT).
        init_linear_gpt2(fc_up, 0.02f, rng);
        const float scale = 1.0f / std::sqrt(2.0f * static_cast<float>(n_layers));
        init_linear_gpt2(fc_down, 0.02f * scale, rng);

        // Move everything to device (uses to_cuda_ which modifies in-place)
        fc_up.to(device);
        fc_down.to(device);
        ln.to(device);

        register_module(ln);
        register_module(fc_up);
        register_module(fc_down);
    }
    
    // Forward: x [B, T, C] -> [B, T, C]
    // Tensor forward(const Tensor& x) override {
    //     // Pre-Norm: ln(x)
    //     Tensor h = ln.forward(x);
        
    //     // Up projection + GELU + Down projection
    //     // Fused: matmul(h, weight) then bias+gelu in one kernel (saves 1 kernel fwd + 1 bwd)
    //     h = autograd::matmul(h, fc_up.weight);
    //     h = autograd::fused_bias_gelu(h, fc_up.bias);
    //     h = fc_down.forward(h);
        
    //     // Residual connection: x + MLP(x)
    //     return autograd::add(x, h);
    // }
    
    Tensor forward(const Tensor& x) override {
        PREC_DUMP(name, "fwd_in", x);
        // Pre-Norm: ln(x)
        Tensor h_ln = ln.forward(x);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".ln_2", x, h_ln);

        Tensor h_up = fc_up.forward(h_ln);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".c_fc", h_ln, h_up);

        Tensor h_gelu = autograd::gelu(h_up);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".gelu", h_up, h_gelu);

        Tensor h_down = fc_down.forward(h_gelu);
        PREC_DUMP_IO(name + ".c_proj", h_gelu, h_down);

        // Residual connection: x + MLP(x)
        Tensor out = autograd::add(x, h_down);
        PREC_DUMP(name, "fwd_out", out);
        return out;
    }
private:
    int64_t n_embd_;
};

// =============================================================================
// GPT Model
// =============================================================================

class GPT : public nn::Module {
public:
    GPTConfig config;
private:
    // MUST be declared before wte/wpe — C++ initializes members in declaration
    // order, and wte/wpe's initializers reference init_rng_, so it has to exist
    // first. Holds the single shared std::mt19937 advanced through every
    // parameter init in gpt2.py's _init_weights traversal order.
    InitRng init_rng_;
public:
    Embedding wte;  // Token embedding [vocab_size, n_embd]
    Embedding wpe;  // Position embedding
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Attention>> attn_blocks;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<MLP>> mlp_blocks;
    nn::LayerNorm ln_f; // Final LayerNorm
    std::shared_ptr<nn::Linear> lm_head;  // Output projection [n_embd, vocab_size], bias=False
                                            // When weight_tying: shares wte.weight (transposed view)
                                            // When no weight_tying: independent weight

    GPT(GPTConfig cfg, DeviceIndex device, uint64_t seed = 1234)
        : config(cfg),
          // Single torch.manual_seed(1234)-style stream advanced through every
          // parameter draw in gpt2.py's apply(_init_weights) traversal order:
          //   wte → wpe → per block (c_attn, attn.c_proj, mlp.c_fc, mlp.c_proj)
          //              → lm_head  (overwrites wte when weight_tying=true)
          // (LayerNorms left at default weight=1 / bias=0 — _init_weights in
          // gpt2.py doesn't touch them either.)
          init_rng_(seed),
          wte(cfg.vocab_size, cfg.n_embd, device, init_rng_, "wte"),
          wpe(cfg.context_length, cfg.n_embd, device, init_rng_, "wpe"),
          ln_f(cfg.n_embd)
    {
        ln_f.to(device);

        // Each block advances the same RNG: c_attn → attn.c_proj → mlp.c_fc → mlp.c_proj.
        for (int i = 0; i < cfg.n_layers; ++i) {
            std::string blk = "h." + std::to_string(i);
            auto a = std::make_shared<Attention>(cfg.n_embd, cfg.n_heads, cfg.n_layers, device, init_rng_,
                                                 blk + ".attn");
            auto m = std::make_shared<MLP>(cfg.n_embd, cfg.n_layers, device, init_rng_,
                                           blk + ".mlp");
            attn_blocks.push_back(a);
            mlp_blocks.push_back(m);
            register_module(a.get());
            register_module(m.get());
        }

        if (!config.weight_tying) {
            // Untied: lm_head is its own parameter — final draw from the same stream,
            // std=0.02 (no NANOGPT_SCALE_INIT, matching gpt2.py's lm_head init).
            lm_head = std::make_shared<nn::Linear>(cfg.n_embd, cfg.vocab_size, false);
            init_linear_gpt2(*lm_head, 0.02f, init_rng_, true);
            lm_head->to(device);
        } else {
            // Tied: in gpt2.py, `self.transformer.wte.weight = self.lm_head.weight`
            // makes both names refer to the same Parameter, and apply(_init_weights)
            // walks lm_head LAST → its Linear normal_(std=0.02) draw OVERWRITES the
            // earlier wte Embedding init in the shared parameter. Replicate by
            // drawing one more value from the shared stream and copy_-ing into
            // wte.weight (preserves tensor identity → registered param + DDP stay
            // valid).
            Tensor lm_head_init = init_rng_.normal(wte.weight.shape(), 0.02f);
            wte.weight.copy_(lm_head_init);
        }

        // Optimization: cache position tensor once (avoids re-creating + H2D transfer every forward)
        Tensor pos_cpu(Shape{{1, cfg.context_length}}, TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Int64));
        int64_t* pos_data = pos_cpu.data<int64_t>();
        for (int64_t i = 0; i < cfg.context_length; ++i) {
            pos_data[i] = i;
        }
        cached_pos_ = pos_cpu.to(device);

        register_module(wte);
        register_module(wpe);
        // attn_blocks and mlp_blocks already registered in the loop above
        register_module(ln_f);
        if (!config.weight_tying && lm_head) {
            register_module(lm_head.get());
        }
    }
    
    // Forward: indices [B, T] -> logits [B, T, vocab_size]
    Tensor forward(const Tensor& idx) override {
        // Get embeddings [B, T, C]
        // std::cout << "Started GPT forward" << std::endl;
        // auto stats = CachingCUDAAllocator::instance().get_stats();
        // std::cout << "Stats reserved before: " << stats.allocated_current / (1024 * 1024) << std::endl;
        Tensor tok_emb = wte.forward(idx);      // [B, T, C]
        
        int64_t T = idx.shape().dims[1];

        // Zero-copy view for position indices (avoids 3 intermediate tensor allocations)
        Tensor pos_indices = (T == config.context_length)
            ? cached_pos_                          // [1, context_length] — reuse directly
            : cached_pos_.narrow_view(1, 0, T);    // [1, T] view — no copy
        Tensor pos_emb = wpe.forward(pos_indices);  // [1, T, C] - broadcasts
        // std::cout << "Pos embedding forward completed" << std::endl;        
        // Add embeddings
        Tensor x = autograd::add(tok_emb, pos_emb);
        PREC_DUMP("emb", "fwd_out", x);
        // std::cout << "add embedding completed" << std::endl;   
        // Transformer blocks: interleave Attention + MLP per layer
        for (int i = 0; i < config.n_layers; ++i) {
            // std::cout << "Transformer forward start: " << i << std::endl; 
            x = attn_blocks[i]->forward(x);  // pre-norm + multi-head attention + residual
            x = mlp_blocks[i]->forward(x);   // pre-norm + FFN + residual
            // std::cout << "Transformer forward completed: " << i << std::endl; 
        }
        // std::cout << "final norm started "<< std::endl;
        // Final normalization
        Tensor x_pre_lnf = x;
        x = ln_f.forward(x);
        PREC_DUMP_IO("ln_f", x_pre_lnf, x);
        // std::cout << "final norm ended "<< std::endl;
        // std::cout << "lm_head started "<< std::endl;

        // Output projection
        Tensor logits;
        if (config.weight_tying) {
            // Tied: reuse wte.weight transposed. autograd::transpose keeps TransposeBackward
            // attached so gradient flows back to wte.weight.AccumulateGrad automatically.
            Tensor w_T = autograd::transpose(wte.weight, 0, 1);
            logits = autograd::matmul(x, w_T);
        } else {
            logits = lm_head->forward(x);  // [B, T, vocab_size]
        }
        PREC_DUMP("lm_head", "fwd_out", logits);
        // std::cout << "Came Here twice" << std::endl;
        // std::cout << "lm_head completed "<< std::endl;
        // std::cout << "Stats reserved after: " << stats.allocated_current / (1024 * 1024) << std::endl;

        
        return logits;
    }

private:
    Tensor cached_pos_;  // [1, T] position indices, cached on GPU
};

// =============================================================================
// Learning Rate Scheduler
// =============================================================================

float get_lr(int step, float MAX_LR, float MIN_LR, int WARMUP_STEPS, int MAX_STEPS) {
    if (step < WARMUP_STEPS) {
        return MAX_LR * static_cast<float>(step + 1) / static_cast<float>(WARMUP_STEPS);
        
    }
    if (step > MAX_STEPS) {
        return MIN_LR;
    }
    float decay_ratio = static_cast<float>(step - WARMUP_STEPS) / static_cast<float>(MAX_STEPS - WARMUP_STEPS);
    float coeff = 0.5f * (1.0f + std::cos(M_PI * decay_ratio));
    return MIN_LR + coeff * (MAX_LR - MIN_LR);
}

// =============================================================================
// Named-parameter list for PrecLogger — names match PyTorch's named_parameters()
// output with the leading "transformer." prefix stripped. Built in the same
// traversal order as the C++ register_module() calls so the index ordering
// also stays aligned with model.parameters().
// =============================================================================

static std::vector<std::pair<std::string, Tensor>> build_named_params(GPT& m) {
    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, Tensor>> out;
    out.emplace_back("wte.weight", m.wte.weight);
    out.emplace_back("wpe.weight", m.wpe.weight);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < m.attn_blocks.size(); ++i) {
        std::string b = "h." + std::to_string(i) + ".";
        // Per gpt2.py Block: ln_1, attn(c_attn, c_proj), ln_2, mlp(c_fc, c_proj).
        out.emplace_back(b + "ln_1.weight",       m.attn_blocks[i]->ln.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "ln_1.bias",         m.attn_blocks[i]->ln.bias);
        out.emplace_back(b + "attn.c_attn.weight", m.attn_blocks[i]->c_attn.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "attn.c_attn.bias",   m.attn_blocks[i]->c_attn.bias);
        out.emplace_back(b + "attn.c_proj.weight", m.attn_blocks[i]->c_proj.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "attn.c_proj.bias",   m.attn_blocks[i]->c_proj.bias);
        out.emplace_back(b + "ln_2.weight",       m.mlp_blocks[i]->ln.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "ln_2.bias",         m.mlp_blocks[i]->ln.bias);
        out.emplace_back(b + "mlp.c_fc.weight",    m.mlp_blocks[i]->fc_up.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "mlp.c_fc.bias",      m.mlp_blocks[i]->fc_up.bias);
        out.emplace_back(b + "mlp.c_proj.weight",  m.mlp_blocks[i]->fc_down.weight);
        out.emplace_back(b + "mlp.c_proj.bias",    m.mlp_blocks[i]->fc_down.bias);
    }
    out.emplace_back("ln_f.weight", m.ln_f.weight);
    out.emplace_back("ln_f.bias",   m.ln_f.bias);
    if (!m.config.weight_tying && m.lm_head) {
        out.emplace_back("lm_head.weight", m.lm_head->weight);
    }
    return out;
}

// =============================================================================
// Init parity loader: read gpt2_init.bin produced by dump_init.py and copy_
// values straight into the model's parameter tensors. Lets the C++ trainer
// start from the EXACT same point in parameter space as gpt2.py at seed=1234,
// removing RNG-stream divergence as a source of drift in like-for-like
// comparisons. Activated via INIT_FROM_BIN=<path>.
//
// Wire format (must match dump_init.py):
//   magic         : 4 bytes "GP2I"
//   version       : uint32 (=1)
//   num_tensors   : uint32
//   per tensor:
//     name_len    : uint16
//     name        : utf-8 bytes
//     dtype       : uint8 (0 = float32)
//     ndim        : uint8
//     dims        : int64 * ndim
//     payload     : float32 * numel
//
// Names use PyTorch's nesting (h.{i}.ln_1, h.{i}.attn.c_attn, ...). The C++
// model has a different structure (LayerNorms live INSIDE Attention/MLP, not
// in a Block), so the loader maps PyTorch names → the matching C++ tensors:
//   ln_1     ↔ attn_blocks[i]->ln       (pre-attn norm)
//   c_attn   ↔ attn_blocks[i]->c_attn
//   attn.c_proj ↔ attn_blocks[i]->c_proj
//   ln_2     ↔ mlp_blocks[i]->ln        (pre-mlp norm)
//   mlp.c_fc ↔ mlp_blocks[i]->fc_up
//   mlp.c_proj ↔ mlp_blocks[i]->fc_down
// Linear weights are already transposed in the file ([in, out]) — the C++
// tensor lib stores Linear as [in, out], so this is a flat memcpy.
// =============================================================================
static void load_init_bin(GPT& model, const std::string& path, bool is_master) {
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: cannot open " + path);

    char magic[4];
    f.read(magic, 4);
    if (std::memcmp(magic, "GP2I", 4) != 0)
        throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: bad magic in " + path);

    uint32_t version = 0, num_tensors = 0;
    f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&version), 4);
    f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&num_tensors), 4);
    if (version != 1u)
        throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: unsupported version");

    // Build name → Tensor& map for the C++ model.
    std::unordered_map<std::string, Tensor*> name_to_tensor;
    name_to_tensor.reserve(2 + 12 * static_cast<size_t>(model.config.n_layers) + 2);
    name_to_tensor["wte.weight"] = &model.wte.weight;
    name_to_tensor["wpe.weight"] = &model.wpe.weight;
    name_to_tensor["ln_f.weight"] = &model.ln_f.weight;
    name_to_tensor["ln_f.bias"]   = &model.ln_f.bias;
    for (int i = 0; i < model.config.n_layers; ++i) {
        const std::string p = "h." + std::to_string(i) + ".";
        auto& a = *model.attn_blocks[i];
        auto& m = *model.mlp_blocks[i];
        name_to_tensor[p + "ln_1.weight"]        = &a.ln.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "ln_1.bias"]          = &a.ln.bias;
        name_to_tensor[p + "attn.c_attn.weight"] = &a.c_attn.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "attn.c_attn.bias"]   = &a.c_attn.bias;
        name_to_tensor[p + "attn.c_proj.weight"] = &a.c_proj.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "attn.c_proj.bias"]   = &a.c_proj.bias;
        name_to_tensor[p + "ln_2.weight"]        = &m.ln.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "ln_2.bias"]          = &m.ln.bias;
        name_to_tensor[p + "mlp.c_fc.weight"]    = &m.fc_up.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "mlp.c_fc.bias"]      = &m.fc_up.bias;
        name_to_tensor[p + "mlp.c_proj.weight"]  = &m.fc_down.weight;
        name_to_tensor[p + "mlp.c_proj.bias"]    = &m.fc_down.bias;
    }
    // Untied lm_head — registered only when present, so dump_init.py is free
    // to either include or omit it. With weight tying, dump_init.py writes
    // the lm_head draw into wte.weight directly (matches gpt2.py's
    // apply(_init_weights) traversal), so the file carries no lm_head entry.
    if (!model.config.weight_tying && model.lm_head) {
        name_to_tensor["lm_head.weight"] = &model.lm_head->weight;
    }

    size_t loaded = 0, total_floats = 0;
    std::vector<float> buf;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < num_tensors; ++i) {
        uint16_t name_len = 0;
        f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&name_len), 2);
        std::string name(name_len, '\0');
        f.read(&name[0], name_len);

        uint8_t dtype = 0, ndim = 0;
        f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&dtype), 1);
        f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&ndim), 1);
        if (dtype != 0)
            throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: only float32 supported, " + name);

        std::vector<int64_t> dims(ndim);
        for (uint8_t d = 0; d < ndim; ++d) {
            f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&dims[d]), 8);
        }
        size_t numel = 1;
        for (auto d : dims) numel *= static_cast<size_t>(d);
        buf.resize(numel);
        f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(buf.data()), numel * sizeof(float));
        if (!f) throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: read failed at " + name);

        auto it = name_to_tensor.find(name);
        if (it == name_to_tensor.end()) {
            if (is_master) std::cerr << "[init-load] WARN: unknown tensor name '" << name
                                     << "' — skipping" << std::endl;
            continue;
        }
        Tensor* dst = it->second;

        // Shape sanity. Both libs store the same logical layout per the
        // load-side mapping above (Embedding [vocab,emb], Linear [in,out]
        // post-transpose, LayerNorm [d]).
        const auto& dst_shape = dst->shape().dims;
        if (static_cast<int64_t>(dst_shape.size()) != static_cast<int64_t>(ndim)) {
            throw std::runtime_error("load_init_bin: ndim mismatch for " + name);
        }
        for (size_t d = 0; d < dst_shape.size(); ++d) {
            if (dst_shape[d] != dims[d]) {
                std::ostringstream oss;
                oss << "load_init_bin: shape mismatch for " << name
                    << " — file says [";
                for (size_t k = 0; k < dims.size(); ++k) oss << dims[k] << (k + 1 < dims.size() ? "," : "");
                oss << "], model has [";
                for (size_t k = 0; k < dst_shape.size(); ++k) oss << dst_shape[k] << (k + 1 < dst_shape.size() ? "," : "");
                oss << "]";
                throw std::runtime_error(oss.str());
            }
        }

        // CPU staging tensor → copy_ pushes to the destination's device.
        Shape shape;
        shape.dims = std::vector<int64_t>(dims.begin(), dims.end());
        Tensor cpu_t(shape, TensorOptions().with_dtype(Dtype::Float32));
        cpu_t.set_data<float>(buf.data(), numel);
        // copy_ requires the destination's req_grad to be off when the source
        // is a fresh leaf tensor (mirrors how init_linear_gpt2 turns req_grad
        // OFF, copy_'s, then turns it back ON). Embedding/Linear weights have
        // req_grad already true here. Toggle around the copy_.
        const bool was_req = dst->requires_grad();
        if (was_req) dst->set_requires_grad(false);
        dst->copy_(cpu_t);
        if (was_req) dst->set_requires_grad(true);

        ++loaded;
        total_floats += numel;
    }

    if (is_master) {
        std::cout << "[init-load] loaded " << loaded << " / " << num_tensors
                  << " tensors (" << total_floats << " floats, "
                  << (total_floats * sizeof(float)) / (1024 * 1024) << " MiB) from "
                  << path << std::endl;
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// Main Training Loop
// =============================================================================

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
    int rank = 0, world_size = 1;
    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &world_size);
    const bool is_master = (rank == 0);

    // PrecLogger writes a shared on-disk tree — keep it master-only by
    // disabling the env on non-master ranks before the singleton observes it.
    if (!is_master) {
        unsetenv("PREC_DUMP_DIR");
    }

    // Runtime SDPA path selector. Default: unfused (baseline).
    // Set USE_PACKED_SDPA=1 to enable scaled_dot_product_attention_packed.
    if (const char* env = std::getenv("USE_PACKED_SDPA")) {
        g_use_packed_sdpa = (env[0] == '1');
    }
    // Within the unfused path: USE_QKV_RESHAPE_FIRST=1 reshapes qkv to
    // [B,T,H,3d] (free view) before sharding axis 3, eliminating the 3
    // contiguous copies the original shard-axis-2 → reshape route forces.
    if (const char* env = std::getenv("USE_QKV_RESHAPE_FIRST")) {
        g_use_qkv_reshape_first = (env[0] == '1');
    }
    if (is_master) {
        std::cout << "Attention path: ";
        if (g_use_packed_sdpa) {
            std::cout << "PACKED-QKV (fused SDPA)";
        } else {
            std::cout << "Zero Call SDPA (shard axis 2 + reshape + transpose + SDPA)";
        }
        std::cout << std::endl;
    }

        // autograd::GraphRecordGuard niggesh(true, "jebam.txt");
        // autograd::g_shape_debug = true;
    
    
    // ---- One GPU per rank ----
    cudaSetDevice(rank);
    DeviceIndex device(Device::CUDA, rank);
    // Skip process group / DDP entirely on single-GPU to avoid the wrapper's overhead.
    std::shared_ptr<ProcessGroupNCCL> pg;
    if (world_size > 1) {
        pg = init_process_group(world_size, rank);
    }
    // Configuration
    GPTConfig config;
    config.context_length = 1024;
    config.vocab_size = 50304;
    config.n_embd = 768;
    config.n_layers = 12;
    config.n_heads = 12;       // Proper multi-head attention
    config.weight_tying = true;
    config.checkpointing = false; // Toggle weight tying Here
    config.if_log = true;
    
    // Training hyperparameters (NanoGPT speedrun — matches gpt2.py)
    const int B = 16;          // Micro batch size (per rank)
    const int T = 1024;        // Sequence length
    const int GLOBAL_BATCH = 524288;  // 2**19, ~0.5M tokens (total across ranks)
    const int GRAD_ACCUM_STEPS = GLOBAL_BATCH / (B * T * world_size);

    const float MAX_LR = 6e-4f;
    const float MIN_LR = MAX_LR * 0.1f;

    // const int WARMUP_STEPS = 715;
   // const int MAX_STEPS = 19073;  // ~1 epoch on 10B tokens at 0.5M batch

    const int WARMUP_STEPS = 715;
    const int MAX_STEPS = 19073;  // ~1 epoch on 10B tokens at 0.5M batch

    const int VAL_FREQ = 250;
    const int TOK_GEN_FREQ = 5000;
    const int CKPT_FREQ = 5000;

    // Target loss thresholds for speedrun timing (NanoGPT target)
    const float TARGET_TRAIN_LOSS = 3.28f;
    const float TARGET_VAL_LOSS = 3.28f;
    if(is_master){
        std::cout << "Configuration:" << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  vocab_size: " << config.vocab_size << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  context_length: " << config.context_length << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  n_embd: " << config.n_embd << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  n_heads: " << config.n_heads << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  n_layers: " << config.n_layers << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  head_dim: " << (config.n_embd / config.n_heads) << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  B=" << B << ", T=" << T << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  GLOBAL_BATCH: " << GLOBAL_BATCH << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  GRAD_ACCUM_STEPS: " << GRAD_ACCUM_STEPS << std::endl;
        std::cout << "  Weight Tying: " << (config.weight_tying ? "ENABLED" : "DISABLED") << std::endl;
    }
    
    std::cout << "\nInitializing model on CUDA device " << rank << "..." << std::endl;
    
    // Create model
    GPT model(config, device);

    // Optional init parity: if INIT_FROM_BIN points at a gpt2_init.bin produced
    // by dump_init.py (same seed, same vocab, same weight_tying), overwrite the
    // in-process random init with the dumped values. This makes the C++ trainer
    // start from the EXACT same point in parameter space as gpt2.py — eliminates
    // RNG-stream divergence between std::mt19937 and torch's RNG as a source of
    // drift in like-for-like comparisons.
    if (const char* p = std::getenv("INIT_FROM_BIN")) {
        if (p[0] != '\0') {
            try {
                load_init_bin(model, p, is_master);
            } catch (const std::exception& e) {
                if (is_master) std::cerr << "[init-load] FATAL: " << e.what() << std::endl;
                MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 2);
            }
            // Init-parity DIAG: dump first 8 floats of two parameters so the
            // load can be byte-compared against dump_init.py's manifest. Master
            // only — every rank loads the same file so values match.
            if (is_master) {
                Tensor wte_cpu = model.wte.weight.to_cpu();
                const float* w = wte_cpu.data<float>();
                std::cout << "[DIAG] wte.weight first 8: ";
                for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
                    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << w[i] << " ";
                std::cout << std::endl;

                Tensor c0_cpu = model.attn_blocks[0]->c_attn.weight.to_cpu();
                const float* c = c0_cpu.data<float>();
                std::cout << "[DIAG] h.0.attn.c_attn.weight first 8: ";
                for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
                    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << c[i] << " ";
                std::cout << std::endl;
            }
        }
    }

    // Named-parameter list (PyTorch-aligned names) for PrecLogger dumps.
    auto named_params = build_named_params(model);

    // Print parameter count
    auto params = model.parameters();
    int64_t num_params = 0;
    for(auto& p : params) num_params += p.numel();

    for(auto& p: params){
        p.display();
    }

    std::unique_ptr<DataParallel> ddp_model;
    if (world_size > 1) {
        DDP_Options ddp_opts;
        ddp_opts = ddp_opts
            .with_process_group(pg)
            .with_world_size(world_size)
            .with_bucket_data(/*bucket=*/true, /*bucket_size_bytes=*/25 * 1024 * 1024)
            .with_grad_view(false);

        ddp_model = std::make_unique<DataParallel>(&model, ddp_opts, /*init_sync=*/false);
        // DDP broadcast just overwrote wte.weight with rank 0's values —
    }

    if(is_master) std::cout << "Number of parameters: " << num_params << std::endl;
    if (!config.weight_tying && is_master) {
        std::cout << "(Note: More params than weight-tied version due to separate lm_head)" << std::endl;
    }
    
    // Create optimizer — single AdamW with wd=0 over ALL params; decoupled weight
    // decay is applied manually below to dim>=2 params only (matches
    // gpt2.py:configure_optimizers — LayerNorm scales and biases never decayed).
    //
    // Two AdamW instances would race on multi_tensor_adam_cuda's static pinned
    // host metadata buffers (h_metadata_A/B/C/D, h_offsets in
    // MultiTensorKernels.cu): the second step()'s host memcpy clobbers the
    // first's source buffer before its async H2D has run. Forcing a sync
    // between the two step() calls fixes correctness but wrecks throughput,
    // so we keep a single step() and do the decay ourselves outside.
    const float WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1f;
    std::vector<Tensor> decay_params;
    decay_params.reserve(params.size());
    int64_t n_decay = 0, n_nodecay = 0;
    for (const auto& p : params) {
        if (p.shape().dims.size() >= 2) {
            decay_params.push_back(p);
            n_decay += p.numel();
        } else {
            n_nodecay += p.numel();
        }
    }
    if (is_master) {
        std::cout << "num decayed parameter tensors: " << decay_params.size()
                  << ", with " << n_decay << " parameters" << std::endl;
        std::cout << "num non-decayed parameter tensors: "
                  << (params.size() - decay_params.size())
                  << ", with " << n_nodecay << " parameters" << std::endl;
    }
    nn::AdamW optimizer(params, MAX_LR, 0.9f, 0.95f, 1e-8f, 0.0f);
    
    // Create data loaders
    std::string data_root = "/mnt/volgrp03/3rd_floor/edu_fineweb10B_bin";
    DataLoaderLite train_loader(B, T, rank, world_size, "train", data_root, true, 100000000, rank);
    DataLoaderLite val_loader(B, T, rank, world_size, "val", data_root, true, 100000000, rank);

    // Data identity diagnostic: dump first 32 input tokens from rank 0's first
    // batch, then reset so training itself is unaffected. Compare against the
    // PyTorch run's matching dump to confirm both pipelines see identical bytes.
    if (is_master) {
        Batch diag = train_loader.next_batch();
        Tensor diag_cpu = diag.input.to_cpu();
        const uint16_t* p = diag_cpu.data<uint16_t>();
        std::cout << "[DIAG] first 32 input tokens (rank 0): ";
        for (int i = 0; i < 32; ++i) std::cout << p[i] << " ";
        std::cout << std::endl;
    }
    train_loader.reset();

    /* ITER4 diagnostic — commented out (reverted).
    // When DUMP_LOGITS=1, run a single forward on rank 0 with
    // the first training batch, dump logits as raw float32 to logits_dump.bin,
    // then exit. Used to bit-diff BluBLAS vs cuBLAS forward outputs.
    if (const char* dump_env = std::getenv("DUMP_LOGITS"); dump_env && dump_env[0] == '1') {
        if (is_master) {
            autograd::NoGradGuard no_grad;
            Batch diag_batch = train_loader.next_batch();
            Tensor diag_logits = model.forward(diag_batch.input);
            Tensor logits_cpu = diag_logits.to_cpu();
            const auto& dims = logits_cpu.shape().dims;
            int64_t numel = logits_cpu.numel();
            std::cout << "[DUMP] logits shape: [";
            for (size_t i = 0; i < dims.size(); ++i) {
                std::cout << dims[i] << (i + 1 < dims.size() ? "," : "");
            }
            std::cout << "] numel=" << numel << " bytes=" << (numel * 4) << std::endl;
            std::ofstream f("logits_dump.bin", std::ios::binary);
            f.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(logits_cpu.data<float>()), numel * sizeof(float));
            f.close();
            const float* lg = logits_cpu.data<float>();
            std::cout << "[DUMP] first 8 logits: ";
            std::cout << std::scientific << std::setprecision(8);
            for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) std::cout << lg[i] << " ";
            std::cout << std::endl;
            double sum = 0.0, sumsq = 0.0;
            float mn = lg[0], mx = lg[0];
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < numel; ++i) {
                sum += lg[i]; sumsq += (double)lg[i] * lg[i];
                if (lg[i] < mn) mn = lg[i];
                if (lg[i] > mx) mx = lg[i];
            }
            double mean = sum / numel;
            std::cout << "[DUMP] mean=" << mean
                      << " sumsq=" << sumsq
                      << " min=" << mn << " max=" << mx << std::endl;
        }
        MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);
        MPI_Finalize();
        return 0;
    }
    */

    /* ITER4 diagnostic (DUMP_GRADS) — commented out (reverted).
    // When DUMP_GRADS=1, run forward + loss + backward on rank 0 with the first
    // training batch, then dump the wte.weight gradient (which IS the lm_head dW
    // under weight tying) and exit. Used to bit-diff the backward pass between
    // BluBLAS and cuBLAS to localize the convergence drift.
    if (const char* dg_env = std::getenv("DUMP_GRADS"); dg_env && dg_env[0] == '1') {
        if (is_master) {
            for (auto& p : params) {
                if (void* g = p.grad()) cudaMemsetAsync(g, 0, p.nbytes());
            }
            cudaDeviceSynchronize();

            Batch diag_batch = train_loader.next_batch();
            Tensor diag_logits = model.forward(diag_batch.input);
            Tensor diag_loss = autograd::sparse_cross_entropy_loss(diag_logits, diag_batch.target);
            Tensor loss_cpu_pre = diag_loss.to_cpu();
            std::cout << "[DUMPG] loss before backward = "
                      << std::scientific << std::setprecision(8)
                      << loss_cpu_pre.data<float>()[0] << std::endl;
            diag_loss.backward();
            cudaDeviceSynchronize();

            Tensor wte_grad_cpu = model.wte.weight.grad_view().to_cpu();
            const auto& gd = wte_grad_cpu.shape().dims;
            int64_t gn = wte_grad_cpu.numel();
            std::cout << "[DUMPG] wte.grad shape: [";
            for (size_t i = 0; i < gd.size(); ++i)
                std::cout << gd[i] << (i + 1 < gd.size() ? "," : "");
            std::cout << "] numel=" << gn << std::endl;
            std::ofstream gf("wte_grad_dump.bin", std::ios::binary);
            gf.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(wte_grad_cpu.data<float>()), gn * sizeof(float));
            gf.close();

            const float* gp = wte_grad_cpu.data<float>();
            std::cout << "[DUMPG] first 8 grads: ";
            for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) std::cout << gp[i] << " ";
            std::cout << std::endl;
            double sum = 0.0, sumsq = 0.0;
            float mn = gp[0], mx = gp[0];
            for (int64_t i = 0; i < gn; ++i) {
                sum += gp[i]; sumsq += (double)gp[i] * gp[i];
                if (gp[i] < mn) mn = gp[i];
                if (gp[i] > mx) mx = gp[i];
            }
            double mean = sum / gn;
            double l2 = std::sqrt(sumsq);
            std::cout << "[DUMPG] mean=" << mean
                      << " sumsq=" << sumsq
                      << " l2_norm=" << l2
